title.raw: 卷一百八十四 列傳第一百三十四: 宦官 Volume 184 Biographies 134: Imperial Officials

sentences.zh: 序善父母爲孝，善兄弟爲友。

translations.literal: In the preface: being good to parents is filial piety; being good to brothers is fraternal friendship.
translations.idiomatic: The preface defines devotion to one's parents as filial piety and kindness toward one's brothers as brotherly friendship.

sentences.zh: 夫善於父母，必能隱身錫類，仁惠逮於胤嗣矣；

translations.literal: One who is good to parents will surely be able to conceal his person and bestow benefits on his kind, and kindness and grace will reach his descendants;
translations.idiomatic: Those who honor their parents invariably shield others of their kind and extend beneficence that reaches even their descendants.

sentences.zh: 善於兄弟，必能因心廣濟，德信被於宗族矣！

translations.literal: One good to brothers will surely be able, from the heart, to extend aid broadly, and virtue and trust will cover the clan!
translations.idiomatic: Those who treat their brothers well spread charity from the heart, and their virtue and trustworthiness envelop the entire clan.

sentences.zh: 推而言之，可以移於君，施於有政，承上而順下，令終而善始，雖蠻貊猶行焉，雖窘迫猶亨焉！

translations.literal: Extending this and speaking of it, it can be transferred to the ruler, applied in government, receiving above and complying below, ending well and beginning well—even among barbarians it would still be practiced, even in distress there would still be prosperity!
translations.idiomatic: Extended further, such conduct can be turned toward one's sovereign and applied in governance—honoring superiors, guiding subordinates, finishing as well as one began—so that even among barbarians it would be honored, and even in hardship one would still flourish.

sentences.zh: 自昔立身揚名，未有不偕孝友而成者也。

translations.literal: From antiquity, establishing oneself and making one's name known—there has never been any who succeeded without together possessing filial piety and brotherly friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, no one who established a lasting reputation did so without filial piety and fraternal harmony together.

sentences.zh: 前代史官，所傳《孝友傳》，多録當時旌表之士，人或微細，非眾所聞，事出閭里，又難詳究。

translations.literal: The historians of former ages, in the transmitted 'Biographies of Filial Piety and Friendship,' mostly recorded men who were honored and marked at the time; the persons were sometimes humble and not heard of by the multitude; the affairs arose in lanes and hamlets, and again are hard to investigate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynastic histories, in their accounts of filial and fraternal exemplars, mostly recorded contemporaries who received official commendation—often humble figures unknown to the wider public, whose deeds arose in village life and are difficult to verify in detail.

sentences.zh: 今録衣冠盛德，眾所知者，以爲稱首。

translations.literal: Now we record eminent virtue among the officer class, those known to the multitude, to serve as the leading examples.
translations.idiomatic: This account therefore begins with celebrated men of official rank whose virtue was widely known.

sentences.zh: 至於州縣薦飾者，必覆其殊尤，可以勸世者，亦載之。

translations.literal: As for those recommended and ornamented by prefectures and counties, we must re-examine their extraordinary excellence; those who can admonish the age—we also record them.
translations.idiomatic: When local officials recommended lesser figures, we verified their exceptional conduct and included only those whose examples could truly instruct society.

sentences.zh: 李知本李知本，趙州元氏人，後魏洛州刺史靈六世孫也。

translations.literal: Li Zhiben—Li Zhiben was a native of Yuanshi in Zhao Prefecture, a sixth-generation descendant of Ling, regional governor of Luo in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhiben, a native of Yuanshi in Zhao Prefecture, was a sixth-generation descendant of Li Ling, who had served as governor of Luo under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父孝端，隋獲嘉丞。

translations.literal: His father Xiaoduan was assistant magistrate of Huojia under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Xiaoduan had been assistant magistrate of Huojia during the Sui.

sentences.zh: 初，孝端與族弟太沖，俱有世閥，而太沖官宦最高，孝端方之爲劣。

translations.literal: Initially, Xiaoduan and his clansman cousin Taichong both came from eminent houses, but Taichong's official career was highest while Xiaoduan considered himself inferior by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: In their youth, Xiaoduan and his clansman Li Taichong both came from distinguished families, but Taichong's official career outshone Xiaoduan's, and Xiaoduan felt himself the lesser.

sentences.zh: 鄕族爲之語，曰：「太沖無兄，孝端無弟。

translations.literal: The villagers said of them: 'Taichong has no elder brother, Xiaoduan has no younger brother.'
translations.idiomatic: Their neighbors would say, "Taichong has no elder brother, and Xiaoduan has no younger brother."

sentences.zh: 」知本頗涉經史，事親至孝，與弟知隱甚稱雍睦。

translations.literal: Zhiben was fairly versed in the classics and histories; in serving his parents he reached the utmost filial piety, and with his younger brother Zhiyin he was greatly praised for harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiben was well read in the classics and histories, served his parents with exemplary filial devotion, and was renowned for harmonious relations with his younger brother Zhiyin.

sentences.zh: 子孫百餘口，財物僮僕，纖毫無間。

translations.literal: Among descendants and dependents there were over a hundred mouths; in property, servants, and trifles there was not the slightest division.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred descendants and dependents shared their household without the slightest division of property, servants, or belongings.

sentences.zh: 隋末，盜賊過其閭而不入，因相讓曰：「無犯義門。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui, when bandits passed their hamlet they would not enter, saying to each other as they yielded way: 'Do not violate the Gate of Righteousness.'
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, bandits passing their neighborhood would not enter, telling one another, "Do not violate the Gate of Righteousness."

sentences.zh: 」同時避難者五百餘家，皆賴而獲免。

translations.literal: Over five hundred families taking refuge at the same time all relied on them and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred families who sought refuge there at the same time were spared through their protection.

sentences.zh: 知本貞觀初官至夏津令，知隱至伊闕丞。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan reign Zhiben rose to Magistrate of Xiajin and Zhiyin to Assistant Magistrate of Yique.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan era, Zhiben became magistrate of Xiajin and Zhiyin assistant magistrate of Yique.

sentences.zh: 知本孫瑱，開元中爲給事中、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhiben's grandson Zhen, in the Kaiyuan era, served as Attendant Censor and prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiben's grandson Zhen served during the Kaiyuan reign as an attendant censor and prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 知隱孫颙，有文詞，亦歷給事中、太常少卿。

translations.literal: Zhiyin's grandson Yong had literary talent and also served as Attendant Censor and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyin's grandson Yong was a gifted writer who likewise served as an attendant censor and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 從祖兄弟，凡爲給事者四人。

translations.literal: Among paternal cousins, four in all served as Attendant Censors.
translations.idiomatic: Among their paternal cousins, four men in all held the post of attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 張志寬張志寬，蒲州安邑人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhikuan—Zhang Zhikuan was a native of Anyi in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhikuan was a native of Anyi in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋末喪父，哀毀骨立，爲州里所稱。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui he lost his father; his mourning was so severe his frame was bone-thin, and the district praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died at the end of the Sui, his grief was so extreme that he wasted to skin and bone, and the whole district praised him.

sentences.zh: 賊帥王君廓屢爲寇掠，聞其名，獨不犯其閭，鄰里賴之而免者百餘家。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Wang Junguo repeatedly raided as a marauder; hearing Zhikuan's name, he alone did not violate his hamlet; over a hundred neighboring families were spared through relying on him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leader Wang Junguo raided repeatedly, but hearing Zhikuan's name he alone spared that neighborhood, and more than a hundred neighboring families were saved through relying on him.

sentences.zh: 後爲里正，詣縣稱母疾，急求歸。

translations.literal: Later as hamlet head he went to the county and claimed his mother was ill, urgently begging to return.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while serving as hamlet head, he went to the county office and reported that his mother was ill, urgently requesting leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 縣令問其狀，對曰：「母嘗有所苦，志寬亦有所苦。

translations.literal: The magistrate asked his condition; he replied: 'When Mother once suffered distress, Zhikuan also suffered distress.'
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate asked what was wrong; he replied, "Whenever my mother suffers, I suffer too."

sentences.zh: 向患心痛，知母有疾。

translations.literal: Just now my heart ached—I knew Mother was ill.
translations.idiomatic: My heart has just been aching, so I knew my mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 」令怒曰：「妖妄之辭也！

translations.literal: The magistrate angrily said: 'This is deluded nonsense!'
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate angrily said, "That is deluded nonsense!"

sentences.zh: 」繫之於獄。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhikuan thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 馳驗其母，竟如所言。

translations.literal: They galloped to verify his mother, and it was exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Messengers were sent at once to check on his mother, and matters were exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 令異之，慰喻遣去。

translations.literal: The magistrate was astonished, comforted and instructed him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate was astonished, comforted him, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 及丁母憂，負土成墳，廬於墓側，手植松柏千餘株。

translations.literal: When he completed mourning for his mother, he carried earth to form the tomb mound, lodged in a hut beside the grave, and planted over a thousand pine and cypress trees by hand.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he carried earth to build her tomb, lived in a mourning hut beside the grave, and planted more than a thousand pine and cypress trees with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，遣使就弔，授員外散騎常侍，賜物四十段，表其門閭。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard of it, sent an envoy to offer condolences on the spot, appointed him Supernumerary Palace Attendant, granted forty lengths of goods, and marked his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu heard of this, sent an envoy to offer condolences, appointed him supernumerary palace attendant, granted him forty lengths of silk, and had his gate and lane officially commended.

sentences.zh: 劉君良劉君良，瀛州饒陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Junliang—Liu Junliang was a man of Raoyang in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Junliang was a native of Raoyang in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累代義居，兄弟雖至四從，皆如同氣，尺布斗粟，人無私焉。

translations.literal: For generations his family lived together in righteousness; though brothers extended to the fourth remove, all were as from one womb—in cloth and grain no one was selfish.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had lived together in harmony; even cousins of the fourth remove were as close as full brothers, and no one kept a private share of cloth or grain.

sentences.zh: 大業末，天下饑饉，君良妻勸其分析，乃竊取庭樹上鳥雛，交置諸巢中，令群鳥鬬競。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, when all under heaven suffered famine, Junliang's wife urged dividing the household; she secretly took fledglings from the courtyard trees and placed them in one another's nests, causing the flock of birds to fight.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign, when famine spread across the empire, Junliang's wife urged him to divide the household; she secretly moved fledglings among the nests in the courtyard trees until the birds were fighting one another.

sentences.zh: 舉家怪之，其妻曰：「方今天下大亂，爭鬬之秋，禽鳥尚不能相容，況於人乎！

translations.literal: The whole family wondered at it; his wife said: 'Now all under heaven is in great disorder, an age of strife—even birds cannot tolerate one another, how much less men!'
translations.idiomatic: The whole family was puzzled, until his wife said, "The empire is in chaos and strife is everywhere—even birds cannot live in peace together; how much less can men!"

sentences.zh: 」君良從之。

translations.literal: Junliang assented.
translations.idiomatic: Junliang agreed.

sentences.zh: 分別後月餘，方知其計。

translations.literal: A month and more after the separation they learned it was her scheme.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month after they had divided the household, they learned it had been her scheme.

sentences.zh: 中夜，遂攬妻髮大呼曰：「此即破家賊耳！

translations.literal: In the middle of the night he seized his wife's hair and cried loudly: 'This is the thief who would break the family!'
translations.idiomatic: In the middle of the night he seized his wife by the hair and cried out, "This is the villain who would destroy our family!"

sentences.zh: 」召諸昆弟，哭以告之。

translations.literal: He summoned all his brothers and, weeping, told them.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned all his brothers and, weeping, told them what had happened.

sentences.zh: 是夜棄其妻，更與諸兄弟同居處，情契如初。

translations.literal: That night he abandoned his wife and again lived together with his brothers; their affection was as at first.
translations.idiomatic: That same night he cast off his wife and rejoined his brothers in a single household, their bond as close as before.

sentences.zh: 屬盜起，閭里依之爲堡者數百家，因名爲義成堡。

translations.literal: When bandits arose, several hundred families in the neighborhood relied on them as a fortified settlement, hence named Righteousness-Fulfilled Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose up, several hundred neighboring families took refuge in their compound, which came to be called Righteousness-Fulfilled Fort.

sentences.zh: ，深州別駕楊弘業造其第，見有六院，唯一飼，子弟數十人，皆有禮節，咨嗟而去。

translations.literal: Shen Prefecture Vice-Prefect Yang Hongye visited his residence, saw six courtyards with but one kitchen, dozens of sons and nephews all with propriety, sighed in admiration and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hongye, vice-prefect of Shen Prefecture, visited his home and saw six courtyards sharing a single kitchen, with dozens of sons and nephews all observing proper decorum; he sighed in admiration and left.

sentences.zh: ，詔加旌表。

translations.literal: An edict added commendation and marking.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict added official commendation to his gate.

sentences.zh: 附 宋興貴又有宋興貴者，雍州萬年人。

translations.literal: Appended: Song Xinggui. There was also Song Xinggui, a man of Wannian in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Song Xinggui. There was also a man named Song Xinggui, a native of Wannian in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累世同居，躬耕致養，至興貴已四從矣。

translations.literal: For generations they lived together, farming to support the family; by Xinggui's time they had reached the fourth remove.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived together for generations, supporting themselves by farming; by Xinggui's day they had reached the fourth degree of cousinship.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘉之，，詔曰：

translations.literal: Gaozu heard and commended him; an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu heard of this and commended him, issuing an edict that read:

sentences.zh: 人稟五常，仁義爲重；

translations.literal: Man receives the Five Constants; benevolence and righteousness are weightiest;
translations.idiomatic: Human beings are endowed with the Five Constants, of which benevolence and righteousness are foremost;

sentences.zh: 士有百行，孝敬爲先。

translations.literal: the gentleman has a hundred conduct-points; filial respect comes first.
translations.idiomatic: and the cultivated man has a hundred virtues, among which filial respect comes first.

sentences.zh: 自古哲王，經邦致治，設教垂範，皆尚於斯。

translations.literal: From antiquity the wise kings, ordering the state and achieving governance, establishing teaching and handing down models—all honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, wise rulers who governed the realm and established moral instruction have all held these principles supreme.

sentences.zh: 叔世澆訛，人多偽薄，修身克己，事資誘勸。

translations.literal: In decadent ages customs are thin and corrupt; men are mostly false and shallow; cultivating the person and restraining the self—the affair relies on inducement and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: In degenerate ages customs grow corrupt and men grow false and shallow; self-cultivation therefore depends on guidance and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 朕恭膺靈命，撫臨四海，湣茲弊俗，方思遷導。

translations.literal: We reverently received the numinous mandate, comfort and oversee the four seas, pity this corrupt custom, and are just now thinking to transform and guide it.
translations.idiomatic: We have reverently received Heaven's mandate and rule the four seas; pitying these corrupt customs, We now seek to transform and guide them.

sentences.zh: 宋興貴立操雍和，志情友穆，同居合爨，累代積年，務本力農，崇謙履順。

translations.literal: Song Xinggui established conduct that was harmonious and mild; in will and feeling he was friendly and reverent; they lived together and shared the cooking hearth for generations accumulated over years; he devoted himself to the root and labored in agriculture, honoring humility and practicing compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xinggui has conducted himself with harmonious dignity, cherishing brotherly affection; his family has lived and cooked together for generations, devoted to farming and humble obedience.

sentences.zh: 弘長名教，敦勵風俗，宜加褒顯，以勸將來。

translations.literal: He expands and lengthens the name-teaching, thickens and encourages customs and manners—he should receive added praise and display, to encourage those yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: He enlarges the reach of moral teaching and strengthens public custom; he should receive special commendation to encourage others in future generations.

sentences.zh: 可表其門閭，蠲免課役。

translations.literal: His gate and lane may be marked; levies and corvée may be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Let his gate be officially commended and his taxes and labor service remitted.

sentences.zh: 布告天下，使明知之。

translations.literal: Proclaim this throughout the realm so that all clearly know it.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed throughout the realm so that all may know it clearly.

sentences.zh: 興貴尋卒。

translations.literal: Xinggui soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 附 張公藝鄆州壽張人張公藝，九代同居。

translations.literal: Appended: Zhang Gongyi of Shouzhang in Yan Prefecture—Zhang Gongyi, nine generations living together.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Zhang Gongyi of Shouzhang in Yan Prefecture lived with nine generations under one roof.

sentences.zh: 北齊時，東安王高永樂詣宅慰撫旌表焉。

translations.literal: In Northern Qi times, Prince of Dong'an Gao Yongle visited the residence to comfort, soothe, and mark and commend them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Northern Qi, Prince Gao Yongle of Dong'an visited his home to offer consolation and had his gate officially commended.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，大使、邵陽公梁子恭亦親慰撫，重表其門。

translations.literal: In Sui Kaihuang, the commissioner, Duke of Shaoyang Liang Zigong, also personally comforted and soothed them, and again marked their gate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign of the Sui, the imperial commissioner Liang Zigong, Duke of Shaoyang, likewise visited in person and had his gate commended again.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，特敕吏加旌表。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, a special edict ordered officials to add commendation and marking.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, a special edict ordered further official commendation for his household.

sentences.zh: 麟德中，高宗有事泰山，路過鄆州，親幸其宅，問其義由。

translations.literal: In Linde, Gaozong had business at Mount Tai; passing through Yan Prefecture he personally visited his residence and asked the reason for his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the Linde era, Emperor Gaozong, traveling to Mount Tai for the feng sacrifice, passed through Yan Prefecture, visited Gongyi's home in person, and asked how his family maintained such harmony.

sentences.zh: 其人請紙筆，但書百餘「忍」字。

translations.literal: The man requested paper and brush and wrote only more than a hundred characters for 'forbearance.'
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi asked for paper and brush and wrote only the character for "forbearance" more than a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 高宗爲之流涕，賜以縑帛。

translations.literal: Gaozong wept for him and granted silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept at this and granted him silk.

sentences.zh: 王君操王君操，萊州即墨人也。

translations.literal: Wang Juncao—Wang Juncao was a man of Jimo in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Juncao was a native of Jimo in Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 其父隋大業中與鄕人李君則鬥競，因被毆殺。

translations.literal: His father, in Sui Daye, had a quarrel with his townsman Li Junze and was beaten to death on that account.
translations.idiomatic: His father had quarreled with a townsman named Li Junze during the Daye reign of the Sui and was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 君操時年六歳，其母劉氏告縣收捕，君則棄家亡命，追訪數年弗獲。

translations.literal: Juncao was then six years old; his mother Lady Liu reported to the county to arrest and seize him; Junze abandoned his family and fled for his life; they pursued and sought him for years without obtaining him.
translations.idiomatic: Juncao was then six years old; his mother, Lady Liu, reported the crime to the county, but Junze fled and could not be found despite years of searching.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，君則自以世代遷革，不慮國刑，又見君操孤微，謂其無復仇之志，遂詣州府自首。

translations.literal: In early Zhenguan, Junze himself thought the generations had changed and did not fear state punishment; seeing Juncao orphaned and slight, he judged him to have no further will for revenge, and so went to the prefectural office to surrender himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan era, Junze assumed that the change of dynasty meant he need not fear prosecution, and seeing Juncao orphaned and powerless, believed he no longer harbored thoughts of revenge; he therefore surrendered himself at the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 而君操密袖白刃刺殺之，刳腹取其心肝，啖食立盡，詣刺史具自陳告。

translations.literal: But Juncao secretly hid a bare blade in his sleeve, stabbed and killed him, cut open the belly and took out his heart and liver, ate them on the spot until finished, and went to the prefect to report everything himself.
translations.idiomatic: Juncao, however, had concealed a dagger in his sleeve; he stabbed Junze to death, cut open his belly, removed his heart and liver, and devoured them on the spot before going to the prefect to confess everything.

sentences.zh: 州司以其擅殺戮，問曰：「殺人償死，律有明文，何方自理，以求生路？

translations.literal: The prefectural office, because he had killed on his own authority, asked: 'Killing a man is repaid with death—the law has clear text; by what reasoning do you explain yourself, seeking a path to life?'
translations.idiomatic: Because he had taken the law into his own hands, the prefectural authorities asked him, "The law plainly requires death for murder—what defense do you offer in hope of saving your life?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「亡父被殺，二十餘載。

translations.literal: He replied: 'My deceased father was killed more than twenty years ago.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "My father was murdered more than twenty years ago."

sentences.zh: 聞諸典禮，父仇不可同天。

translations.literal: I have heard in the canonical rites that a father's enemy cannot share the same sky.
translations.idiomatic: According to the rites, a father's enemy cannot live under the same heaven as his son.

sentences.zh: 早願圖之，久而未遂，常懼亡滅，不展冤情。

translations.literal: Long ago I wished to plot it, but for long I did not succeed; I constantly feared extinction and could not unfold my grievance.
translations.idiomatic: I long wished to avenge him but could not; I constantly feared I would die before my wrong could be righted.

sentences.zh: 今大恥既雪，甘從刑憲。

translations.literal: Now the great shame has been wiped away; I gladly submit to punishment under the law.
translations.idiomatic: Now that this great shame is wiped away, I willingly accept whatever punishment the law requires.

sentences.zh: 」州司據法處死，列上其狀，太宗特詔原免。

translations.literal: The prefectural office sentenced him to death according to law and submitted a report of the case upward; Taizong specially issued an edict pardoning and exempting him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural office sentenced him to death according to law and reported the case upward, but Emperor Taizong issued a special edict pardoning him.

sentences.zh: 附 周智壽、智爽周智壽者，雍州同官人。

translations.literal: Appended: Zhou Zhishou and Zhishuang. Zhou Zhishou was a man of Tongguan in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Zhou Zhishou and Zhou Zhishuang. Zhou Zhishou was a native of Tongguan in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其父永徽初被族人安吉所害。

translations.literal: His father, in early Yonghui, was killed by his clansman Anji.
translations.idiomatic: His father had been killed in the early Yonghui era by a clansman named Anji.

sentences.zh: 智壽及弟智爽乃候安吉於途，擊殺之。

translations.literal: Zhishou and his younger brother Zhishuang then waited for Anji on the road and struck and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishou and his younger brother Zhishuang lay in wait for Anji on the road and killed him.

sentences.zh: 兄弟相率歸罪於縣，爭爲謀首，官司經數年不能決。

translations.literal: The brothers together led one another to surrender guilt at the county, each contending to be the chief plotter; the officials for years could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers went together to the county to surrender, each claiming to have been the chief instigator, and the authorities could not decide the case for years.

sentences.zh: 鄕人或證智爽先謀，竟伏誅。

translations.literal: Someone in the village testified that Zhishuang had plotted first; in the end he suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Some townspeople testified that Zhishuang had planned the killing first, and he was eventually executed.

sentences.zh: 臨刑神色自若，顧謂市人曰：「父仇已報，死亦何恨！

translations.literal: Facing execution his expression was calm; turning to the people in the market he said: 'My father's enemy is already avenged—what regret is there in death!'
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution he remained calm and said to the crowd, "My father's enemy is avenged—what regret is there in death!"

sentences.zh: 」智壽頓絶衢路，流血遍體。

translations.literal: Zhishou collapsed in the middle of the street, blood flowing over his whole body.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishou collapsed in the middle of the street, blood streaming over his whole body.

sentences.zh: 又收智爽屍，舐取智爽血，食之皆盡，見者莫不傷焉。

translations.literal: He then gathered Zhishuang's corpse, licked and took Zhishuang's blood, ate it all, and those who saw it were without exception grieved.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered his brother's corpse, licked up Zhishuang's blood, and consumed it all; all who witnessed this were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 附 許坦豫州人許坦，年十歳餘，父入山采藥，爲猛獸所噬，即號叫以杖擊之，獸遂奔走，父以得全。

translations.literal: Appended: Xu Tan of Yuzhou. Xu Tan, a little over ten years old—his father entered the mountains to gather medicine and was seized by a fierce beast; he immediately cried out and struck it with a staff; the beast then fled, and his father was thereby preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Xu Tan of Yuzhou. When Xu Tan was a little over ten, his father went into the mountains to gather herbs and was attacked by a wild beast; the boy cried out and beat the animal with a staff until it fled, and his father was saved.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而謂侍臣曰：「坦雖幼童，遂能致命救親，至孝自中，深可嘉尚。

translations.literal: Taizong heard and said to his attending ministers: 'Though Tan is a young child, he was able to risk his life to save his parent; utmost filial piety arose from within—deeply worthy of praise and esteem.'
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of this, he told his ministers, "Though Tan is only a child, he risked his life to save his father—such filial devotion arising from the heart is deeply admirable."

sentences.zh: 」授文林郎，賜帛五十段。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Forest of Literature and granted fifty lengths of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed gentleman of the Forest of Literature and granted fifty lengths of silk.

sentences.zh: 附 王少玄博州聊城人王少玄者，父隋末於郡西爲亂兵所害。

translations.literal: Appended: Wang Shaoxuan of Liaocheng in Bozhou. Wang Shaoxuan—his father at the end of the Sui west of the commandery was killed by disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Wang Shaoxuan of Liaocheng in Bozhou. His father had been killed by marauding soldiers west of the commandery at the end of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 少玄遺腹生，年十餘歳，問父所在。

translations.literal: Shaoxuan was born after his father's death; at a little over ten years he asked where his father was.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxuan was born after his father's death; when he was a little over ten, he asked where his father was.

sentences.zh: 其母告之，因哀泣，便欲求屍以葬。

translations.literal: His mother told him; he thereupon wept in grief and at once wished to seek the corpse for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother told him, he wept in grief and at once set out to find his father's body for burial.

sentences.zh: 時白骨蔽野，無由可辨。

translations.literal: At the time white bones covered the wilds; there was no means to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: White bones lay scattered across the countryside, and there was no way to tell which were his father's.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「以子血霑父骨，即滲入焉。

translations.literal: Someone said: 'If a son's blood is applied to his father's bones, it will seep in.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone told him, "If a son's blood touches his father's bones, it will be absorbed."

sentences.zh: 」少玄乃刺其體以試之。

translations.literal: Shaoxuan then pierced his body to test this.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxuan then pierced his own flesh to test this.

sentences.zh: 凡經旬日，竟獲父骸以葬。

translations.literal: In all it took more than ten days; in the end he obtained his father's remains and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days of searching, he finally found his father's remains and buried them.

sentences.zh: 盡體病瘡，歷年方愈。

translations.literal: His whole body was afflicted with sores; only after years did he recover.
translations.idiomatic: His whole body was covered with sores and took years to heal.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，本州聞薦，拜除王府參軍。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, the home prefecture heard and recommended him; he was appointed and dismissed as staff officer of a princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, his prefecture recommended him, and he was appointed staff officer in a princely household.

sentences.zh: 趙弘智趙弘智，洛州新安人。

translations.literal: Zhao Hongzhi—Zhao Hongzhi was a native of Xin'an in Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hongzhi was a native of Xin'an in Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 後魏車騎大將軍肅孫。

translations.literal: Grandson of Su, General of Chariots and Cavalry of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was a grandson of Zhao Su, who had served as general of chariots and cavalry under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父玄軌，隋陜州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xuangu was prefect of Shanzhou under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao Xuangu had been prefect of Shanzhou during the Sui.

sentences.zh: 弘智早喪母，事父以孝聞。

translations.literal: Hongzhi lost his mother early; in serving his father he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi lost his mother at an early age and became renowned for filial devotion to his father.

sentences.zh: 學通《三禮》、《史記》、《漢書》。

translations.literal: In learning he mastered the Three Rites, the Records of the Grand Historian, and the Book of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Three Rites, the Records of the Grand Historian, and the Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，爲司隸從事。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, he served as an aide in the Office of the Intendant of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era of the Sui, he served as an aide in the metropolitan intendant's office.

sentences.zh: 武德初，大理卿郎楚之應詔舉之，授詹事府主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, Minister of Justice Lang Chuzhi, responding to an imperial decree, recommended him; he was appointed chief clerk of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude reign, Minister of Justice Lang Chuzhi recommended him by imperial summons, and he was appointed chief clerk in the heir apparent's household administration.

sentences.zh: 又預修《六代史》。

translations.literal: He also participated in compiling the History of the Six Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in compiling the History of the Six Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 初，與秘書丞令狐德棻、齊王文學袁朗等十數人同修《藝文類聚》，轉太子舍人。

translations.literal: Initially, together with Secretariat Director Linghu Defen, Prince of Qi Literary Companion Yuan Lang, and more than ten others, he jointly compiled the Collection of Literary Treasures; he was transferred to become aide to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, he joined Secretariat Director Linghu Defen, Literary Companion to the Prince of Qi Yuan Lang, and more than ten others in compiling the Collection of Literary Treasures, and was then transferred to the post of aide to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累遷黃門侍郎，兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, through successive promotions he became Vice Minister of the Secretariat and concurrently a scholar of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, he rose through successive promotions to vice minister of the secretariat and concurrently served as a scholar of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 以疾出爲萊州刺史。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was sent out to become prefect of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he was sent out to serve as prefect of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 弘智事兄弘安，同於事父，所得俸祿，皆送於兄處。

translations.literal: Hongzhi served his elder brother Hong'an as he would serve a father; all salary he received he sent to his brother.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi treated his elder brother Hong'an as he would a father, sending him every penny of his official salary.

sentences.zh: 及兄亡，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: When his elder brother died, his grief and emaciation exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother died, his grief and self-mortification went beyond what the rites required.

sentences.zh: 事寡嫂甚謹，撫孤侄以慈愛稱。

translations.literal: In serving his widowed sister-in-law he was very careful; in raising his orphaned nephew he was known for kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was scrupulously devoted to his widowed sister-in-law and was praised for the loving care with which he raised his orphaned nephew.

sentences.zh: 稍遷太子右庶子。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to right assistant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 及宮廢，坐除名。

translations.literal: When the palace establishment was abolished, on account of it he was stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent's household was abolished, he was dismissed and stripped of rank on account of it.

sentences.zh: 尋起爲光州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was recalled to become prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to serve as prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，累轉陳王師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, through successive transfers he became tutor to the Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yonghui reign, he was transferred in succession to become tutor to the Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 高宗令弘智於百福殿講《孝經》，召中書門下三品及弘文館學士、太學儒者，並預講筵。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong had Hongzhi lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety at Baifu Hall, summoning third-rank officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Hongwen Academy scholars, and Confucians of the Imperial Academy, all to join the lecture assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had Hongzhi lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety in Baifu Hall, summoning third-rank officials of the secretariat and chancellery, Hongwen Academy scholars, and Confucians of the Imperial Academy, all of whom joined the lecture.

sentences.zh: 弘智演暢微言，備陳五孝。

translations.literal: Hongzhi eloquently expounded subtle doctrine and fully set forth the five forms of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi expounded the text with eloquence and fully explained the five forms of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 學士等難問相繼，弘智酬應如響。

translations.literal: The scholars' challenging questions followed one after another; Hongzhi's responses came like an echo.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars posed one challenging question after another, and Hongzhi answered each as promptly as an echo.

sentences.zh: 高宗怡然曰：「朕頗耽墳籍，至於《孝經》，偏所習睹。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said with pleasure: 'I am quite devoted to the classics; as for the Classic of Filial Piety, it is one I have especially studied and observed.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said with evident pleasure, "I am quite devoted to the classics, and of the Classic of Filial Piety in particular I have read and studied a great deal."

sentences.zh: 然孝之爲德，弘益實深，故云『德教加於百姓，刑於四海，是知孝道之爲大也。

translations.literal: Yet filial piety as a virtue—its expansive benefit is truly profound; thus it says, 'When moral teaching is applied to the common people, it serves as a model to all within the four seas'—this shows how great filial piety is.
translations.idiomatic: Yet filial piety as a virtue carries benefits that are truly far-reaching; thus it is said, 'When moral teaching is applied to the common people, it serves as a model throughout the four seas'—this shows how great filial piety is.

sentences.zh: 」顧謂弘智：「宜略陳此經切要者，以輔不逮。

translations.literal: Turning to Hongzhi, he said: 'You should briefly set forth the essential points of this classic, to assist where I fall short.'
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Hongzhi, he said, "You should briefly set forth the essential points of this classic to help me where I fall short."

sentences.zh: 」弘智對曰：「昔者天子有諍臣七人，雖無道不失其天下。

translations.literal: Hongzhi replied: 'In antiquity, if a son of Heaven had seven remonstrating ministers, even though he was without the Way he would not lose his realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi replied, "In antiquity, if a ruler had seven ministers who remonstrated with him, even though he lacked the Way he would not lose his realm."

sentences.zh: 微臣顓愚，願以此言奏獻。

translations.literal: This humble subject is specially dull-witted; I wish to offer this saying to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant is especially dull-witted, but I wish to offer this saying for Your Majesty's consideration.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅，賜彩絹二百匹、名馬一匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and granted him two hundred bolts of colored silk and one famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and granted him two hundred bolts of colored silk and one fine horse.

sentences.zh: 尋遷國子祭酒，仍爲崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and continued as a scholar of the Chongxian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to chancellor of the Directorate of Education while continuing to serve as a scholar of the Chongxian Academy.

sentences.zh: 四年卒，年八十二，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, at age eighty-two; his posthumous title was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yonghui he died at the age of eighty-two; his posthumous title was Xuan.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected writings in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 陳集原陳集原，瀧州開陽人也。

translations.literal: Chen Jiyuan—Chen Jiyuan was a native of Kaiyang in Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiyuan was a native of Kaiyang in Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代爲嶺表酋長。

translations.literal: For generations his family were chieftains in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had served as chieftains in the Lingnan region.

sentences.zh: 父龍樹，欽州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Longshu was prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Longshu had been prefect of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 集原幼有孝行，父才有疾，即終日不食。

translations.literal: Jiyuan from youth had filial conduct; whenever his father Cai had an illness, he would go the whole day without eating.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan showed filial conduct from childhood; whenever his father Cai fell ill, he would go the entire day without eating.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，喪父，嘔血數升，枕服苫廬，悲感行路。

translations.literal: In Yonghui, when his father died, he vomited several sheng of blood, wore the mourning pillow and sackcloth hut, and his grief moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign, when his father died, he vomited several pints of blood, slept on the mourning pillow in a thatched hut by the grave, and his grief moved everyone who passed along the road.

sentences.zh: 資財田宅及僮僕三十餘人，並以讓兄弟。

translations.literal: Property, fields, houses, and more than thirty servants—all he yielded to his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He gave over to his brothers all his property, fields, houses, and more than thirty servants.

sentences.zh: 則天時，官至左豹韜衞將軍。

translations.literal: In Wu Zetian's time, he reached the office of general of the Left Leopard and Crossbow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Wu Zetian's reign he rose to the rank of general of the Left Leopard and Crossbow Guard.

sentences.zh: 元讓元讓，雍州武功人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Rang—Yuan Rang was a native of Wugong in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Rang was a native of Wugong in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弱冠明經擢第。

translations.literal: At twenty he passed the classics examination with highest honors.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of twenty he passed the classics examination with highest honors.

sentences.zh: 以母疾，遂不求仕。

translations.literal: Because his mother was ill, he therefore did not seek office.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was ill, he declined to seek office.

sentences.zh: 躬親藥膳，承侍致養，不出閭里者數十餘年。

translations.literal: He personally prepared medicines and meals, attending and nourishing her; for more than twenty years he did not leave his neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: He personally prepared medicines and meals, attending and nourishing her, and for more than twenty years never left his neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 及母終，廬於墓側，蓬髮不櫛沐，菜食飲水而已。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he built a hut beside the tomb, let his hair grow unkempt without combing or washing, and ate vegetables and drank water only.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he built a mourning hut beside her tomb, let his hair grow wild without combing or washing, and subsisted on vegetables and water alone.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，孝敬監國，下令表其門閭。

translations.literal: In Xianheng, when Xiao Jing was regent, he issued an order to honor his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianheng reign, when Crown Prince Xiao Jing was regent, he issued an order honoring Rang's household.

sentences.zh: ，巡察使奏讓孝悌殊異，擢拜太子右內率府長史。

translations.literal: The touring inspector memorialized that Rang's filial piety and brotherliness were exceptionally outstanding; he was promoted and appointed senior steward of the Right Inner Rate Office of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A touring inspector memorialized that Rang's filial piety and brotherly devotion were exceptionally outstanding, and he was promoted to senior steward of the Right Inner Rate Office of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 後以歳滿還鄕里。

translations.literal: Later, when his term expired, he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his term of office expired, he returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 鄕人有所爭訟，不詣州縣，皆就讓決焉。

translations.literal: When villagers had disputes, they did not go to the prefecture or county; all came to Rang for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: When local people had disputes, they did not go to the prefectural or county offices but came to Rang for judgment.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中，中宗居春宮，召拜太子司議郎。

translations.literal: During Shenli, when Zhongzong resided in the Eastern Palace, he was summoned and appointed memorial draftsman of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenli era, when Zhongzong resided in the Eastern Palace, Rang was summoned and appointed memorial draftsman to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 及謁見，則天謂曰：「卿既能孝於家，必能忠於國。

translations.literal: At his audience, Wu Zetian said: 'Since you can be filial at home, you must be able to be loyal to the state.'
translations.idiomatic: At his audience, Wu Zetian said, "Since you can be filial at home, you must be able to be loyal to the state.

sentences.zh: 今授此職，須知朕意。

translations.literal: In appointing you to this office now, you must understand my intent.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing you to this office now, you must understand my intent.

sentences.zh: 宜以孝道輔弼我兒。

translations.literal: You should assist and guide my son with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: You should assist and guide my son with filial devotion."

sentences.zh: 」尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 裴敬彜裴敬彜，絳州聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Jingyi—Pei Jingyi was a native of Wenxi in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jingyi was a native of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖子通，隋開皇中太中大夫。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zitong was a Grand Master for Splendid Happiness in the Kaihuang era of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zitong had served as grand master for splendid happiness during the Kaihuang era of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 母終，廬於墓側，哭泣無節，目遂喪明。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he built a hut beside the tomb, wept without restraint, and eventually lost his sight.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he built a mourning hut beside her tomb, wept without restraint, and eventually lost his sight.

sentences.zh: 俄有白鳥巢於墳樹。

translations.literal: Soon a white bird nested in a tree at the grave.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a white bird nested in a tree at the grave.

sentences.zh: 子通弟兄八人，復以友悌著名，詔旌表其門，鄕人至今稱爲「義門裴氏」。

translations.literal: Zitong's eight brothers were also famous for fraternal friendship; an edict honored their gate, and villagers to this day call them the 'Righteous Gate Pei Clan.'
translations.idiomatic: Zitong's eight brothers were also renowned for brotherly harmony; an edict honored their household, and local people still call them the Righteous Gate Pei clan.

sentences.zh: 敬彜少聰敏，七歳解屬文。

translations.literal: Jingyi from youth was clever; at seven he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi was clever from childhood and could compose literary pieces by the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 性又端謹，宗族咸重之，號爲「甘露頂」。

translations.literal: His nature was also upright and careful; the clan all respected him, calling him 'Sweet Dew Crown.'
translations.idiomatic: He was also upright and conscientious by nature; the whole clan respected him and called him Sweet Dew Crown.

sentences.zh: 年十四，侍御史唐臨爲河北巡察使，敬彜父智周時爲內黃令，爲部人所訟，敬彜詣臨論其冤。

translations.literal: At fourteen, when Censor Tang Lin was touring inspector of Hebei, Jingyi's father Zhizhou was then magistrate of Neihuang and was sued by people under his jurisdiction; Jingyi went to Lin to argue his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of fourteen, when Censor Tang Lin was touring inspector of Hebei, Jingyi's father Zhizhou was serving as magistrate of Neihuang and had been sued by people under his jurisdiction; Jingyi went to Tang Lin to argue his father's innocence.

sentences.zh: 臨大奇之，因令作詞賦。

translations.literal: Lin was greatly amazed and had him compose a rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Lin was greatly impressed and had him compose a rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 智周事得釋，特表薦敬彜，補陳王府典簽。

translations.literal: Zhizhou's case was cleared; Lin specially memorialized recommending Jingyi, who was appointed recorder of the Prince of Chen's household.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhou's case was cleared, and Tang Lin specially memorialized recommending Jingyi, who was appointed recorder in the household of the Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 智周在官暴卒，敬彜時在長安，忽泣涕不食，謂所親曰：「大人毎有痛處，吾即輒然不安。

translations.literal: Zhizhou died suddenly while in office; Jingyi was then in Chang'an and suddenly wept, refused food, and said to those close to him: 'Whenever the elder had a painful ailment, I would at once feel uneasy.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhou died suddenly while in office; Jingyi was then in Chang'an and suddenly burst into tears and refused to eat, telling those close to him, "Whenever my father had a painful ailment, I would immediately feel uneasy."

sentences.zh: 今日心痛，手足皆廢，事在不測，得無戚乎？

translations.literal: Today my heart aches and my hands and feet are both useless; the matter is uncertain—can I not be sorrowful?
translations.idiomatic: Today my heart aches and my hands and feet have gone numb; something unforeseen must have happened—how can I not be filled with dread?"

sentences.zh: 」遂請急還，倍道言歸。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested urgent leave to return and hurried home by double marches.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately requested emergency leave and raced home by forced marches.

sentences.zh: 果聞父喪，羸毀逾禮。

translations.literal: He indeed heard of his father's death; his emaciation from grief exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He indeed learned of his father's death and wasted away in grief beyond what the rites prescribed.

sentences.zh: 事母復以孝聞。

translations.literal: In serving his mother he was again known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his mother he was again renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，累轉監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng, through successive transfers he became supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianfeng reign, he rose through successive transfers to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 時母病，有醫人許仁則，足疾不能乘馬，敬彜毎肩輿之以候母焉。

translations.literal: When his mother was ill, there was a physician Xu Renze whose foot ailment prevented him from riding; Jingyi every day carried him in a sedan chair to attend his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, there was a physician named Xu Renze who could not ride because of a foot ailment; every day Jingyi carried him in a sedan chair to treat his mother.

sentences.zh: 及母卒，特詔贈以縑帛，仍官造靈輿。

translations.literal: When his mother died, a special edict granted silk as a gift, and the government also had a funeral carriage made.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, a special edict granted him silk as a gift, and the government also had a funeral carriage made for the occasion.

sentences.zh: 服闋，拜著作郎，兼修國史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed drafting secretary and concurrently edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he was appointed drafting secretary and concurrently worked on the national history.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，自中書舍人歷吏部侍郎、左庶子。

translations.literal: In Yifeng, from Secretariat Drafter he passed through Vice Minister of Personnel to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng reign, he rose from secretariat drafter through vice minister of personnel to left assistant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，爲酷吏所陷，配流嶺南，尋卒。

translations.literal: When Wu Zetian held court, he was framed by a harsh official and sentenced to exile in Lingnan; soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian took the throne, he was framed by a harsh official, sentenced to exile in Lingnan, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 裴守真裴守真，絳州稷山人也。

translations.literal: Pei Shouzhen—Pei Shouzhen was a native of Jishan in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shouzhen was a native of Jishan in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後魏冀州刺史叔業六世孫也。

translations.literal: He was a sixth-generation descendant of Shuye, governor of Ji Province under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was a sixth-generation descendant of Pei Shuye, who had served as governor of Ji Province under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父慎，大業中爲淮南郡司戸。

translations.literal: His father Shen served as revenue clerk of Huainan Commandery during Daye.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen had served as revenue clerk of Huainan Commandery during the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 屬郡人楊琳、田瓚據郡作亂，盡殺官吏。

translations.literal: When natives of the commandery Yang Lin and Tian Zan seized the commandery and rebelled, they killed all the officials.
translations.idiomatic: When local men Yang Lin and Tian Zan seized the commandery and rebelled, they killed every official.

sentences.zh: 以慎素有仁政，相誡不許驚害，仍令人護送慎及妻子還鄕。

translations.literal: Because Shen had long practiced benevolent governance, they admonished one another not to harm him and still sent men to escort Shen and his wife and children back home.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shen had long governed with benevolence, they warned one another not to harm him and instead sent men to escort Shen and his family safely home.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，官至酂令。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he reached the office of magistrate of Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he rose to the post of magistrate of Zuo.

sentences.zh: 守真早孤，事母至孝。

translations.literal: Shouzhen lost his father early; in serving his mother he was supremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen lost his father at an early age and was supremely filial in serving his mother.

sentences.zh: 及母終，哀毀骨立，殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his grief wasted him to skin and bone; he nearly could not bear the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his grief wasted him to skin and bone, and he nearly succumbed to mourning.

sentences.zh: 復事寡姊及兄甚謹，閨門禮則，士友所推。

translations.literal: He was again very careful in serving his widowed elder sister and elder brother; household ritual propriety was praised by scholar-friends.
translations.idiomatic: He was also scrupulous in serving his widowed elder sister and elder brother, and the ritual propriety of his household won the esteem of friends and scholars.

sentences.zh: 初舉進士，及應八科舉，累轉乾封尉，屬永淳初關中大饑，守真盡以祿俸供姊及諸甥，身及妻子粗糲不充，初無倦色。

translations.literal: Initially he passed the jinshi examination and also responded to the eight-subject examination; through successive transfers he became magistrate of Qianfeng. In the beginning of Yongchun there was great famine in Guanzhong; Shouzhen used all his salary to support his sister and various nephews, while he himself, his wife, and children had coarse food insufficient to fill them, yet from the first he showed no weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He first passed the jinshi examination and also took the eight-subject examination, then rose through successive posts to magistrate of Qianfeng. At the beginning of the Yongchun era, when Guanzhong suffered severe famine, Shouzhen spent his entire salary supporting his sister and nephews, while he, his wife, and children had barely enough coarse food to eat, yet he never showed the least sign of weariness.

sentences.zh: 尋授太常博士。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 守真尤善禮儀之學，當時以爲稱職。

translations.literal: Shouzhen was especially skilled in the study of ritual propriety; at the time he was considered fit for his post.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen was especially skilled in ritual studies and was regarded at the time as thoroughly fit for his office.

sentences.zh: 高宗時封嵩山，詔禮官議射牲之事，守真奏曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong performed the feng rite on Mount Song, he ordered ritual officials to discuss the matter of shooting the sacrificial victim; Shouzhen memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong performed the feng rite on Mount Song, he ordered ritual officials to discuss the shooting of the sacrificial victim; Shouzhen submitted a memorial saying,

sentences.zh: 據《周禮》及《國語》，郊祀天地，天子自射其牲。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou and the Discourses of the States, in suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth the Son of Heaven himself shoots the sacrificial victim.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Rites of Zhou and the Discourses of the States, in suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth the Son of Heaven himself shoots the sacrificial victim.

sentences.zh: 漢武唯封太山，令侍中儒者射牲行事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han, only in sealing Mount Tai, ordered attendant gentlemen and Confucian scholars to shoot the victim and perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han, only when sealing Mount Tai, had attendant gentlemen and Confucian scholars shoot the victim and perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 至於餘祀，亦無射牲之文。

translations.literal: As for the remaining sacrifices, there is likewise no text concerning shooting the victim.
translations.idiomatic: As for other sacrifices, there is likewise no record of shooting the victim.

sentences.zh: 但親舂射牲，雖是古禮，久從廢省。

translations.literal: Yet personally pounding grain and shooting the victim, though ancient rites, have long been abandoned and omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet personally pounding the sacrificial grain and shooting the victim, though ancient rites, have long since fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 據封禪祀禮曰：未明十五刻，宰人以鸞刀割牲，質明而行事。

translations.literal: According to the feng and shan sacrifice rites: before dawn, at the fifteenth notch, the butcher uses the bell-handled knife to cut the victim; at full dawn the rites proceed.
translations.idiomatic: According to the feng and shan sacrifice rites, before dawn at the fifteenth time-mark the butcher uses the bell-handled knife to cut the victim, and at full dawn the rites proceed.

sentences.zh: 比鸞駕至時，宰牲總畢，天皇唯奠玉酌獻而已。

translations.literal: By the time the imperial carriage arrives, butchering is altogether complete; the Emperor only presents jade and pours the libation.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the imperial carriage arrives, butchering is already complete, and the emperor need only present the jade and pour the libation.

sentences.zh: 今祀前一日射牲，事即傷早；

translations.literal: If now the victim is shot on the day before the sacrifice, the matter is harmed by being too early;
translations.idiomatic: If the victim were shot on the day before the sacrifice, the rite would suffer from being too early;

sentences.zh: 祀日方始射牲，事又傷晩。

translations.literal: If on the day of the sacrifice one only then shoots the victim, the matter is again harmed by being too late.
translations.idiomatic: if it were shot only on the day of the sacrifice, the rite would again suffer from being too late.

sentences.zh: 若依漢武故事，即非親射之儀，事不可行。

translations.literal: If one follows the precedent of Emperor Wu of Han, that is not the ceremony of personally shooting; the matter cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: If one followed the precedent of Emperor Wu of Han, that would not be the ceremony of the ruler personally shooting the victim, and the practice cannot be adopted.

sentences.zh: 又《神功破陣樂》、《功成慶善樂》二舞，毎奏，上皆立對。

translations.literal: Again, for the two dances Meritorious Achievement Breaking the Battle Array and Meritorious Achievement Celebrating Good Governance, whenever they were performed the sovereign always stood facing them.
translations.idiomatic: Again, whenever the two dances Meritorious Achievement Breaking the Battle Array and Meritorious Achievement Celebrating Good Governance were performed, the emperor always stood to face them.

sentences.zh: 守真又議曰：

translations.literal: Shouzhen again deliberated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen offered a further opinion, saying,

sentences.zh: 竊唯二舞肇興，謳吟攸屬，贊九功之茂烈，葉萬國之歡心。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that these two dances at their inception belong to songs and chants, praising the abundant achievements of the nine merits, harmonizing the rejoicing hearts of the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that these two dances arose from song and chant, praising the abundant achievements of imperial merit and harmonizing the rejoicing hearts of all nations.

sentences.zh: 義均《韶》、《夏》，用兼賓祭，皆祖宗盛德，而子孫享之。

translations.literal: Their meaning equals the Sha and the Xia; they are used together in guest and sacrifice rites—all are the abundant virtue of ancestors and forebears, enjoyed by descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Their significance equals that of the Sha and Xia music; they are used in both guest and sacrificial rites—all celebrate the great virtue of the imperial ancestors, enjoyed by their descendants.

sentences.zh: 詳覽傳記，未有皇王立觀之禮。

translations.literal: Examining records in detail, there is no rite of an emperor standing to observe.
translations.idiomatic: A careful review of historical records shows no precedent for an emperor standing to observe such a performance.

sentences.zh: 況升中大事，華夷畢集，九服仰垂拱之安，百蠻懷率舞之慶。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the great affair of ascending the central peak, Chinese and barbarians all assemble; the nine domains look up to the ease of ruling with folded hands, and the hundred barbarians cherish the joy of dancing in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at the great ceremony of ascending the central peak, Chinese and foreigners alike will assemble; the nine domains look up to the emperor's tranquil rule, and the hundred barbarian peoples share in the joy of harmonious celebration.

sentences.zh: 甄陶化育，莫匪神功，豈於樂舞，別申嚴敬。

translations.literal: Molding and nurturing through transformation—none is not divine achievement; how in music and dance alone should one separately express solemn reverence?
translations.idiomatic: The molding and nurturing of all under Heaven is entirely the work of imperial merit—why should solemn reverence be expressed separately only in music and dance?

sentences.zh: 臣等詳議，奏二舞時，天皇不合起立。

translations.literal: We have deliberated in detail and conclude that when the two dances are performed, the Emperor should not rise and stand.
translations.idiomatic: After careful deliberation, we conclude that when these two dances are performed, the emperor should not rise and stand.

sentences.zh: 時並從守真議。

translations.literal: At the time all followed Shouzhen's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all agreed with Shouzhen's opinion.

sentences.zh: 會高宗不豫，事竟不行。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Gaozong was unwell, and in the end the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong fell ill, however, and in the end the ceremony was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 及高宗崩，時無大行兇儀，守真與同時博士韋叔夏、輔抱素等討論舊事創爲之，當時稱爲得禮之中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong died, at the time there were no mourning rites for a deceased emperor on the grand journey; Shouzhen, together with fellow erudites Wei Shuxia, Fu Baosu, and others, discussed old precedents and newly created them; at the time they were praised as hitting the mean of ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong died, there were at the time no established mourning rites for a deceased emperor; Shouzhen, together with fellow erudites Wei Shuxia, Fu Baosu, and others, studied old precedents and devised new ones, and at the time their work was praised as striking the proper balance in ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 守真天授中爲司府丞，則天特令推究詔獄，務存平恕，前後奏免數十家。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era, Shouzhen served as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan; Wu Zetian specially ordered him to investigate edict-case prisons, striving to preserve fairness and clemency, and before and after he memorialized the release of several dozen families.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era, Shouzhen served as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan; Empress Wu Zetian specially ordered him to investigate edict-case prisons, striving to preserve fairness and clemency, and before and after he memorialized the release of several dozen families.

sentences.zh: 由是不合旨，出爲汴州司録，累轉成州刺史。

translations.literal: Because of this he did not accord with imperial intent; he was sent out as chief clerk of Bian Prefecture and through successive transfers became governor of Cheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he failed to please the throne; he was sent out as chief clerk of Bian Prefecture and, through successive transfers, became governor of Cheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 爲政不務威刑，甚爲人吏所愛。

translations.literal: In governing he did not rely on severe punishments and was greatly loved by officials and the people.
translations.idiomatic: In office he did not rely on harsh punishments and was greatly loved by officials and the people.

sentences.zh: 俄轉寧州刺史，成州人送出境者數千人。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to governor of Ning Prefecture; several thousand people of Cheng Prefecture escorted him beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor of Ning Prefecture, and several thousand people of Cheng Prefecture escorted him beyond the prefectural border.

sentences.zh: 長安中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Chang'an era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Chang'an era.

sentences.zh: 守真子 子餘子子餘，事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Shouzhen's son Pei Ziyu was known for filial piety in serving his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shouzhen's son Pei Ziyu was renowned for filial devotion to his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，累補鄠縣尉。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination; through successive appointments he became assistant magistrate of E County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and, through successive appointments, became assistant magistrate of E County.

sentences.zh: 時同列李朝隱、程行諶皆以文法著稱，子餘獨以詞學知名。

translations.literal: At the time his colleagues Li Chaoyin and Cheng Xingshen were both distinguished for literary style and law, while Ziyu alone was renowned for literary scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his colleagues Li Chaoyin and Cheng Xingshen were both renowned for literary style and legal expertise, while Ziyu alone was known for literary scholarship.

sentences.zh: 或問雍州長史陳崇業，子餘與朝隱、行諶優劣，崇業曰：「譬如春蘭秋菊，俱不可廢也。

translations.literal: Someone asked Yong Prefecture chief administrator Chen Chongye whether Ziyu or Chaoyin and Xingshen was superior or inferior; Chongye said: "They are like spring orchids and autumn chrysanthemums—neither may be dispensed with."
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Chen Chongye, chief administrator of Yong Prefecture, which was superior, Ziyu or Chaoyin and Xingshen; Chongye replied, "They are like spring orchids and autumn chrysanthemums—neither can be done without."

sentences.zh: 」景龍中，爲左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era, he served as Left Censorate investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era, he served as investigating censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 時涇、岐二州有隋代蕃戸子孫數千家，司農卿趙履溫奏，悉沒爲官戸奴婢，仍充賜口，以給貴幸。

translations.literal: At the time in Jing and Qi prefectures there were several thousand descendants of Sui-era frontier-household dependents; Minister of the Imperial Granaries Zhao Lüwen memorialized that all be confiscated and made government-household slaves and maidservants, still to be assigned as grant-holders to supply the noble and favored.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jing and Qi prefectures held several thousand descendants of Sui-era frontier-household dependents; Minister of the Imperial Granaries Zhao Lüwen memorialized that all be confiscated and made government-household slaves and maidservants, to be distributed as grant-holders among the nobility and favorites.

sentences.zh: 子餘以爲官戸承恩，始爲蕃戸，又是子孫，不可抑之爲賤，奏劾其事。

translations.literal: Ziyu held that government households received imperial favor, had originally been frontier households, and were moreover descendants—they could not be demeaned to low status; he memorialized to impeach the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu argued that government households enjoyed imperial favor, had originally been frontier households, and were moreover descendants—they could not be reduced to base status; he memorialized to impeach the proposal.

sentences.zh: 時履溫依附宗楚客等，與子餘廷對曲直。

translations.literal: At the time Lüwen was attached to Zong Chuke and others; in court he disputed right and wrong with Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lüwen was allied with Zong Chuke and others; in court he debated the rights and wrongs of the matter with Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 子餘詞色不撓，履溫等詞屈，從子餘奏爲定。

translations.literal: Ziyu's words and bearing did not bend; Lüwen and the others were defeated in argument, and Ziyu's memorial was adopted as definitive.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu's words and bearing did not waver; Lüwen and the others were defeated in argument, and Ziyu's memorial was adopted as final.

sentences.zh: 開元初，累遷冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, through successive promotions he became governor of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, he was promoted through successive appointments to governor of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 政存寬惠，人吏稱之。

translations.literal: His governance preserved leniency and kindness; officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was marked by leniency and kindness, and officials and the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 又爲岐王府長史，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He also served as chief administrator of the Prince of Qi's household, with additional rank as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as chief administrator of the Prince of Qi's household and was given the additional rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 十四年卒，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died; posthumous title Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died; his posthumous title was Xiao (Filial).

sentences.zh: 子餘居官清儉，友愛諸兄弟。

translations.literal: Ziyu in office was pure and frugal and affectionately loved all his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu was pure and frugal in office and affectionately devoted to all his brothers.

sentences.zh: 兄弟六人，皆有志行。

translations.literal: Of six brothers, all had aspiration and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: All six brothers had aspiration and integrity.

sentences.zh: 次弟巨卿，衞尉卿；

translations.literal: The next younger brother Juqing was Minister of the Court of Imperial Ceremonial;
translations.idiomatic: The next younger brother, Juqing, was Minister of the Court of Imperial Ceremonial;

sentences.zh: 耀卿，別有傳。

translations.literal: Yaoqing has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoqing has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 李日知李日知，鄭州滎陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Rizhi was a man of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rizhi was a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 天授中，累遷司刑丞。

translations.literal: During Tianshou, through successive promotions he became vice director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era, he was promoted through successive appointments to vice director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時用法嚴急，日知獨寬平，無冤濫。

translations.literal: At the time the application of law was strict and urgent; Rizhi alone was lenient and fair, with no wrongful excess.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the law was applied with strict urgency; Rizhi alone was lenient and fair, and no wrongful punishments occurred under him.

sentences.zh: 嘗免一死囚，少卿胡元禮請斷殺之，與日知往復至於數四。

translations.literal: Once he freed a condemned prisoner; Vice Minister Hu Yuanli requested execution, and he and Rizhi exchanged arguments back and forth up to four times.
translations.idiomatic: Once he freed a prisoner condemned to death; Vice Minister Hu Yuanli demanded execution, and he and Rizhi exchanged arguments back and forth as many as four times.

sentences.zh: 元禮怒，曰：「元禮不離刑曹，此囚終無生理。

translations.literal: Yuanli angrily said: "If Yuanli does not leave the penal office, this prisoner will ultimately have no way to live."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli said angrily, "If Yuanli does not leave the penal office, this prisoner will never live."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「日知不離刑曹，此囚終無死法。

translations.literal: He replied: "If Rizhi does not leave the penal office, this prisoner will ultimately have no way to die."
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi replied, "If Rizhi does not leave the penal office, this prisoner will never die."

sentences.zh: 」因以兩狀列上，日知果直。

translations.literal: Thereupon both memorials were submitted; Rizhi proved correct.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon both memorials were submitted together, and Rizhi proved to be in the right.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，爲給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, he served as chief draft reviser.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, he served as chief draft reviser.

sentences.zh: 日知事母至孝。

translations.literal: Rizhi served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi served his mother with exemplary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 時母老，嘗疾病，日知取急，調侍數日而鬢髮變白。

translations.literal: At the time his mother was old and once fell ill; Rizhi took urgent leave, attended and served for several days, and his temple hair turned white.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his mother was elderly and once fell ill; Rizhi took urgent leave and nursed her for several days until the hair at his temples turned white.

sentences.zh: 尋加朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Soon additionally appointed Grand Master for Dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed Grand Master for Dispersal.

sentences.zh: 其母未受命婦邑號而卒，將葬發引，吏人賫告身而至，日知於路上即時殞絶，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: His mother died before receiving a titled lady's patent; as the funeral procession was setting out, officials carrying the patent of appointment arrived; on the road Rizhi at once collapsed and died, and after a long time revived.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died before receiving a titled lady's patent; as the funeral procession was setting out, officials arrived carrying her patent of appointment, and on the road Rizhi at once collapsed as if dead; only after a long while did he revive.

sentences.zh: 左右皆哀慟，莫能仰視。

translations.literal: Those around him all mourned in grief and could not look up at him.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him all wept in grief and could not bear to look at him.

sentences.zh: 巡察使、衞州司馬路敬潛將聞其孝悌之跡，使求其狀，日知辭讓不報。

translations.literal: Touring inspector and Weizhou vice prefect Lu Jingqian wished to hear of his filial and fraternal conduct and sent to request a formal report; Rizhi declined and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Touring inspector and Weizhou vice prefect Lu Jingqian wished to report his filial and fraternal conduct and sent to request a formal account; Rizhi declined and did not respond.

sentences.zh: 服闋，累遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, through successive promotions he became vice director of the Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he was promoted through successive appointments to vice director of the Gate Guards.

sentences.zh: 時安樂公主池館新成，中宗親往臨幸，從官皆預宴賦詩。

translations.literal: At the time Princess Anle's pool pavilion was newly completed; Emperor Zhongzong personally went to visit, and attendant officials all participated in the banquet and composed poems.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Princess Anle's pool pavilion was newly completed; Emperor Zhongzong personally went to visit it, and all attendant officials joined the banquet and composed poems.

sentences.zh: 日知獨存規誡，其末章曰：「所願暫思居者逸，莫使時稱作者勞。

translations.literal: Rizhi alone preserved admonition; his closing stanza said: "What I wish is briefly to think of the ease of those who dwell—do not let the age call the builders to labor."
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi alone preserved admonition; his closing stanza read, "My wish is briefly to consider the comfort of those who live here—do not let posterity say the builders labored in vain."

sentences.zh: 」論者多之。

translations.literal: Those who commented mostly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators largely praised him for it.

sentences.zh: ，同中書門下平章事，轉御史大夫，知政事如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, transferred to Censor-in-Chief, and continued to handle affairs of state as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, transferred to Censor-in-Chief, and continued to handle affairs of state as before.

sentences.zh: 明年，進拜侍中。

translations.literal: The next year, he was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: ，轉刑部尚書，罷知政事。

translations.literal: He transferred to Minister of Justice and ceased handling affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Justice and removed from handling affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 頻乞骸骨，請致仕，許之。

translations.literal: Repeatedly begging to retire on account of old age, he requested leave of office; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly begged to retire on account of old age and requested leave of office; his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 初，日知將有陳請，而不與妻謀，歸家而使左右飾裝，將出居別業。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Rizhi was about to submit his request but had not consulted his wife, he returned home and had attendants prepare luggage, intending to go out and live at a separate estate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Rizhi was about to submit his request but had not yet consulted his wife, he returned home and had attendants prepare luggage, intending to move to a separate estate.

sentences.zh: 妻驚曰：「家產屢空，子弟名宦未立，何爲遽辭職也？

translations.literal: His wife in alarm said: "Household property is repeatedly empty, sons and nephews' official careers are not yet established—why suddenly resign office?"
translations.idiomatic: His wife said in alarm, "Our household property is nearly gone, and our sons and nephews have not yet established official careers—why resign office so suddenly?"

sentences.zh: 」日知曰：「書生至此，已過本分。

translations.literal: Rizhi said: "A scholar reaching this point has already exceeded his proper share."
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi said, "For a scholar to reach this point has already exceeded his proper share."

sentences.zh: 人情無厭，若恣其心，是無止足之日。

translations.literal: Human desire has no satiety; if one indulges the heart, there will be no day of stopping.
