translations.idiomatic: Human desire knows no limit; if one indulges the heart, there will never be a day of stopping.

sentences.zh: 」及歸田園，不事產業，但葺構池亭，多引後進，與之談宴。

translations.literal: When he returned to fields and gardens, he did not pursue property management, but only repaired and constructed ponds and pavilions, often inviting junior scholars, and feasting and conversing with them.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to his estate, he did not pursue property management but only repaired ponds and pavilions, often inviting younger scholars to feast and converse with them.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 初，日知以官在權要，諸子弟年才總角，皆結婚名族，時議以爲失禮之中。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Rizhi's office was among the powerful, all his younger brothers while still in childhood were married into famous clans; contemporary opinion held this among failures in propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Rizhi held a powerful office, all his younger brothers were married into eminent clans while still children; contemporary opinion counted this among lapses in propriety.

sentences.zh: 卒後，少子伊衡，以妾爲妻，費散田宅，仍列訟諸兄，家風替矣。

translations.literal: After he died, the youngest son Yiheng took a concubine as wife, squandered fields and houses, still brought lawsuits against his elder brothers—the family style declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Rizhi died, his youngest son Yiheng took a concubine as his wife, squandered the family fields and houses, and still brought lawsuits against his elder brothers—the family reputation collapsed.

sentences.zh: 崔沔崔沔，京兆長安人，周隴州刺史士約玄孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Mian was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao, great-grandson of Zhou Prefect of Longxi Shi Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Mian was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao, great-grandson of Zhou Prefect of Longxi Shi Yue.

sentences.zh: 自博陵徙關中，世爲著姓。

translations.literal: Having moved from Boling to the Guanzhong region, for generations they were an eminent surname.
translations.idiomatic: Having moved from Boling to the Guanzhong region, the family had for generations been an eminent clan.

sentences.zh: 父皚，庫部員外郎、汝州長史。

translations.literal: His father Cui Hao was Secretariat clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and chief administrator of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cui Hao was a secretariat clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and chief administrator of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 沔淳謹，口無二言，事親至孝，博學有文詞。

translations.literal: Mian was pure and cautious, never spoke doubly, served his parents with utmost filial piety, and was broadly learned with literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was pure and cautious, never spoke with two meanings, served his parents with exemplary filial devotion, and was broadly learned with literary talent.

sentences.zh: 初應制舉，對策高第。

translations.literal: At first he responded to the decree examination and his policy essay placed in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: At first he responded to the decree examination and his policy essay placed in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 俄被落第者所援，則天令所司重試，沔所對策，又工於前，爲天下第一，由是大知名。

translations.literal: Soon those who failed the examination cited him; Wu Zetian ordered the office to re-examine; Mian's policy essay again surpassed the previous one, ranking first under Heaven; thereby he became greatly renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon those who had failed the examination appealed against him; Wu Zetian ordered the office to re-examine the papers; Mian's policy essay again surpassed his previous one and ranked first in the empire, and thereby he became greatly renowned.

sentences.zh: 再轉陸渾主簿。

translations.literal: Through a second transfer he became chief clerk of Lu Hun.
translations.idiomatic: After a second transfer he became chief clerk of Lu Hun.

sentences.zh: 秩滿調遷，吏部侍郎岑羲深賞重之，謂人曰：「此今之郤詵也。

translations.literal: When his term expired and he was transferred, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Cen Yi deeply valued him and told people: "This is a Xi Shen of our day."
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired and he was transferred, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Cen Yi deeply valued him and told people, "This is a Xi Shen of our day."

sentences.zh: 」特表薦擢爲左補闕，累遷祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: Specially memorialized and promoted to Left Supplementation Censor; through successive promotions he became assistant director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially memorialized and promoted to Left Supplementation Censor and, through successive promotions, became assistant director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 沔爲人舒緩，訥於造次，當官正色，未嘗撓沮。

translations.literal: Mian as a person was easy and unhurried, slow of speech in emergencies; in office he maintained correct demeanor and never bent or faltered.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was by nature easy and unhurried and slow of speech in emergencies; in office he maintained a correct demeanor and never bent or faltered.

sentences.zh: 睿宗時，徵拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: During Ruizong's reign, summoned and appointed Central Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Ruizong's reign he was summoned and appointed a Central Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 時沔母老疾在東都，沔不忍舍之，固請閑官，以申侍養，由是改爲虞部郎中。

translations.literal: At the time Mian's mother was old and ill in the Eastern Capital; Mian could not bear to leave her, firmly requested a leisurely post to attend and nourish her, and thereby was changed to Departmental Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mian's mother was old and ill in the Eastern Capital; unable to leave her, he firmly requested a less demanding post so he could attend and care for her, and was therefore changed to Departmental Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 無何，檢校御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long, acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時監察御史宋宣遠，恃盧懷慎之親，頗犯法，沔舉劾之。

translations.literal: At the time, investigating censor Song Xuanyuan relied on kinship with Lu Huaiyuan and frequently violated the law; Mian memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, investigating censor Song Xuanyuan relied on his kinship with Lu Huaiyuan and frequently violated the law; Mian memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 又姚崇之子光祿少卿彜，留司東都，頗通賓客，廣納賄賂，沔又將按驗其事。

translations.literal: Also Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yao Chong's son Yao Yi, remaining to administer the Eastern Capital, extensively associated with guests and broadly received bribes; Mian again was about to investigate and verify the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Also Yao Chong's son Yao Yi, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, who remained to administer the Eastern Capital, extensively entertained guests and broadly received bribes—Mian again was about to investigate the matter.

sentences.zh: 姚、盧時在政事，遽薦沔有史才，轉爲著作郎，其實去權也。

translations.literal: Yao and Lu were then in office; hastily they recommended Mian had talent for history, transferred him to works director—in reality removing him from power.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Lu were then in office; they hastily recommended that Mian had talent for historical compilation and transferred him to Director of Compilation—in reality removing him from power.

sentences.zh: ，爲太子左庶子。

translations.literal: He served as Left Sub-prefect of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left Sub-prefect of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 母卒，哀毀逾禮，常於廬前受弔，賓客未嘗至於靈座之室，謂人曰：「平生非至親者，未嘗升堂入謁，豈可以存亡而變其禮也。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his mourning grief exceeded the rites; he regularly received condolence visitors at the mourning hut; guests never entered the chamber of the spirit seat; he told people: "In life, except for the closest kin, I never ascended the hall to pay visits—how could one change the rites for life and death?"
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his mourning grief exceeded the rites; he regularly received condolence visitors at the mourning hut, and guests never entered the chamber of the spirit seat; he told people, "In life, except for my closest kin, I never ascended the hall to receive visitors—how could I change my rites because of life and death?"

sentences.zh: 」中書令張説數稱薦之。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Director Zhang Yue repeatedly praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Central Secretariat Director Zhang Yue repeatedly praised and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 服闋，拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, appointed vice director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he was appointed vice director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 或謂沔曰：「今之中書，皆是宰相承宣制命。

translations.literal: Someone said to Mian: "The Central Secretariat today is entirely where chancellors receive and promulgate edict commands."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Mian, "The Central Secretariat today is entirely where chancellors receive and promulgate edict commands."

sentences.zh: 侍郎雖是副貳，但署位而已，甚無事也。

translations.literal: The vice director, though second in rank, only signs his seat—there is very little business.
translations.idiomatic: The vice director, though second in rank, only occupies his seat—there is very little to do.

sentences.zh: 」沔曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Mian said: "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Mian said, "Not so."

sentences.zh: 設官分職，上下相維，各申所見，方爲濟理。

translations.literal: Establish offices and divide duties—superior and subordinate mutually support each other; each expressing what he sees is what makes governance effective.
translations.idiomatic: Offices are established and duties divided so that superior and subordinate mutually support one another; only when each expresses what he sees can governance succeed.

sentences.zh: 豈可俯默偷安，而爲懷祿士也！

translations.literal: How can one bow in silence and steal ease, becoming a salary-seeking gentleman!
translations.idiomatic: How can one bow in silence and steal ease, becoming a man who holds office only for his salary!

sentences.zh: 」自是毎有制敕及曹事，沔多所異同，張説頗不悅焉。

translations.literal: From then on whenever there were edicts or bureau business, Mian often differed in many points; Zhang Yue was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever there were edicts or bureau business, Mian often differed on many points, and Zhang Yue was quite displeased.

sentences.zh: 尋出爲魏州刺史，奏課第一，徵還朝廷，分掌吏部十銓事。

translations.literal: Soon sent out as governor of Wei Prefecture; memorialized first in administrative assessment; summoned back to court, shared charge of ten streams of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as governor of Wei Prefecture, ranked first in administrative assessment, summoned back to court, and given shared charge of ten streams of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以清直，歷秘書監、太子賓客。

translations.literal: Because of pure straightforwardness, successively served as Director of the Secretariat and Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his pure and upright character, he successively served as Director of the Secretariat and Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，制令禮官議加籩豆之數及服制之紀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, an edict ordered rites officials to discuss increasing the number of sacrificial vessels and the categories of mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, an edict ordered rites officials to discuss increasing the number of sacrificial vessels and the categories of mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 太常卿韋縚奏請加宗廟之奠，毎坐籩豆各十二。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Tao memorialized requesting addition to the ancestral temple offerings—at each seat twelve baskets and dou vessels each.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Tao memorialized requesting additional offerings in the ancestral temple—twelve food baskets and twelve standing cups at each seat.

sentences.zh: 外祖服，請加至大功九月，舅服加至小功五月，堂姨、堂舅、舅母服，請加至袒免。

translations.literal: For maternal grandfather mourning, requested extension to ninth-month greater mourning; maternal uncle mourning extended to fifth-month lesser mourning; paternal aunt, paternal uncle's wife, and maternal uncle's wife mourning—all requested extension to barest headband mourning.
translations.idiomatic: For mourning a maternal grandfather, he requested extension to ninth-month greater mourning; for mourning a maternal uncle, extension to fifth-month lesser mourning; and for mourning a paternal aunt, a paternal uncle's wife, and a maternal uncle's wife, extension to barest headband mourning.

sentences.zh: 時又令百官詳議可否。

translations.literal: At the time also ordered all officials to discuss in detail whether feasible or not.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the throne also ordered all officials to discuss in detail whether these proposals were feasible.

sentences.zh: 沔建議曰：

translations.literal: Mian submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Mian submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 竊聞識禮樂之情者能作，達禮樂之文者能述。

translations.literal: I have heard that one who knows the sentiment of ritual and music can create; one who comprehends the text of ritual and music can expound.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that one who knows the sentiment of ritual and music can create it, and one who comprehends the text of ritual and music can expound it.

sentences.zh: 述作之義，聖賢所重；

translations.literal: The meaning of expounding and creating is what sages and worthies value;
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of expounding and creating is what sages and worthies value;

sentences.zh: 禮樂之本，古今所崇。

translations.literal: the root of ritual and music is what ancients and moderns honor.
translations.idiomatic: the root of ritual and music is what ancients and moderns alike honor.

sentences.zh: 變而通之，所以久也。

translations.literal: Transform and adapt—the means by which it endures long.
translations.idiomatic: Transform and adapt—that is how it endures.

sentences.zh: 所謂變者，變其文也；

translations.literal: What is called transformation is transforming its literary form;
translations.idiomatic: What is called transformation is transforming its outward form;

sentences.zh: 所謂通者，通其情也。

translations.literal: what is called adaptation is adapting to its inner sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: what is called adaptation is adapting to its inner sentiment.

sentences.zh: 祭祀之興，肇於太古，人所飲食，必先嚴獻。

translations.literal: Sacrifice arose from most ancient times; what humans eat and drink, they first strictly offer.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice arose in most ancient times; whatever humans eat and drink, they first offer in solemn dedication.

sentences.zh: 未有火化，茹毛飲血，則有毛血之薦；

translations.literal: Before there was fire to cook food, eating raw meat and drinking blood—there were offerings of hair and blood;
translations.idiomatic: Before fire was used to cook food, when people ate raw meat and drank blood, there were offerings of hair and blood;

sentences.zh: 未有曲糵，汙樽抔飲，則有玄酒之奠。

translations.literal: before there was fermented liquor, drinking from muddy vessels with cupped hands—there were offerings of dark wine.
translations.idiomatic: before fermented liquor existed, when people drank from muddy vessels with cupped hands, there were offerings of dark wine.

sentences.zh: 施及後王，禮物漸備，作爲酒醴，伏其犧牲，以致馨香，以極豐潔，故有三牲八簋之盛，五齊九獻之殷。

translations.literal: Extending to later kings, ritual objects gradually became complete; they made wine and ale, killed the sacrificial victims, to send forth fragrant aroma, reaching the utmost abundance—in consequence there are the grandeur of three victims and eight gui, the profusion of five grades of ale and nine offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Extending to later kings, ritual objects gradually became complete; wine and ale were made and sacrificial victims were killed to send forth fragrant aroma and reach the utmost abundance—in consequence there came the grandeur of three victims and eight gui vessels, and the profusion of five grades of ale and nine rounds of offering.

sentences.zh: 然以神道至玄，可存而不可測也；

translations.literal: Yet the spirit way is supremely mysterious—it may be preserved but cannot be measured;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the spirit way is supremely mysterious—it may be honored but cannot be fathomed;

sentences.zh: 祭禮主敬，可備而不敢廢也。

translations.literal: sacrificial rites take reverence as their core—they may be fully provided but dare not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: sacrificial rites take reverence as their core—they may be fully provided for, yet dare not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 是以血腥爛熟，玄樽犧象，靡不畢登於明薦矣！

translations.literal: Therefore raw and cooked blood offerings, dark wine and sacrificial bronze vessels—none fail to be fully presented at the bright offering!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore raw and cooked blood offerings, dark wine, and sacrificial bronze vessels—none fail to be fully presented at the bright offering!

sentences.zh: 然而薦貴於新，味不尚褻，雖則備物，猶存節制。

translations.literal: Yet in offering, freshness is prized; flavor is not prized when defiled—though objects are fully provided, restraint is still preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in offering, freshness is prized and defiled flavors are not honored—though the objects are fully provided, restraint is still preserved.

sentences.zh: 故《禮》云：「天之所生，地之所長，茍可薦者，莫不咸在。

translations.literal: Therefore the Rites says: "What Heaven produces and Earth grows—whatever can be offered, none is not all present.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Rites says: "What Heaven produces and Earth grows—whatever can be offered is all included.

sentences.zh: 」備物之情也。

translations.literal: "—the sentiment of fully providing objects."
translations.idiomatic: "—that is the sentiment of fully providing all offerings."

sentences.zh: 「三牲之俎，八簋之實，美物備矣；

translations.literal: "The stands of the three victims, the contents of the eight gui—fine objects are fully provided;
translations.idiomatic: "The stands of the three victims, the contents of the eight gui—the finest offerings are fully provided;

sentences.zh: 昆蟲之異，草木之實，陰陽之物備矣。

translations.literal: the oddities of insects, the fruits of grasses and trees—the objects of yin and yang are fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: the exotic varieties of insects, the fruits of grasses and trees—all things of yin and yang are fully provided.

sentences.zh: 」此則節制之文也。

translations.literal: "—this is the literary form of restraint."
translations.idiomatic: "—this is the textual expression of restraint."

sentences.zh: 铏俎、籩豆、簠簋、樽罍之實，皆周人之時饌也，其用通於宴饗賓客。

translations.literal: The contents of meat stands, basket-and-cup vessels, grain vessels, and wine jars and goblets—all are the ordinary foods of Zhou people; their use extends to feasting and entertaining guests.
translations.idiomatic: The contents of meat stands, basket-and-cup vessels, grain vessels, and wine jars and goblets were all ordinary foods in the Zhou era, and their use extended to feasts and entertaining guests.

sentences.zh: 而周公制禮，咸與毛血玄酒同薦於先。

translations.literal: Yet when the Duke of Zhou established the rites, all were together offered to the ancestors alongside hair-and-blood and dark wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Duke of Zhou established the rites, all were offered to the ancestors alongside hair-and-blood and dark wine.

sentences.zh: 晉中郎盧諶，近古之知禮、著《家祭禮》者也。

translations.literal: Jin Central Palace Gentleman Lu Chen was one in recent antiquity who knew ritual and wrote the Family Sacrifice Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chen, Central Palace Gentleman of Jin, was among those in recent antiquity who knew ritual and wrote the Family Sacrifice Rites.

sentences.zh: 觀其所薦，皆晉時常食，不復純用禮經舊文。

translations.literal: Observing what he offered, all were ordinary foods of Jin times—no longer purely using the old text of the ritual classics.
translations.idiomatic: Observing what he offered, one finds only ordinary foods of Jin times—no longer relying purely on the old prescriptions of the ritual classics.

sentences.zh: 然則當時飲食，不可闕於祭祀明矣，是變禮文而通其情也！

translations.literal: Thus it is clear that the foods of the time cannot be omitted from sacrifice—this is transforming the literary form of ritual while adapting to its inner sentiment!
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is clear that the foods of one's own time cannot be omitted from sacrifice—this is transforming the outward form of ritual while adapting to its inner sentiment!

sentences.zh: 我國家由禮立訓，因時制範，考圖史於前典，稽周、漢之舊儀。

translations.literal: Our state establishes instruction through ritual, sets standards according to the times, examines charts and histories in earlier classics, and consults the old ceremonies of Zhou and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Our state establishes instruction through ritual and sets standards according to the times, examining charts and histories in earlier classics and consulting the old ceremonies of Zhou and Han.

sentences.zh: 清廟時享，禮饌畢陳，用周制也，而古式存焉；

translations.literal: At the Pure Temple's seasonal offerings, ritual foods are fully displayed—using Zhou institutions, yet ancient forms are preserved therein;
translations.idiomatic: At the Pure Temple's seasonal offerings, ritual foods are fully displayed—the Zhou institutions are used, yet ancient forms are preserved;

sentences.zh: 園寢上食，時膳具設，遵漢法也，而珍味極焉。

translations.literal: At the garden mausoleums' food offerings, timely dishes are fully set out—following Han methods, yet reaching the utmost in delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: At the garden mausoleums' food offerings, timely dishes are fully set out—Han methods are followed, yet delicacies are presented to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 職貢來祭，致遠物也；

translations.literal: Tribute from official duties arrives for sacrifice—presenting objects from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Tribute from official duties arrives for sacrifice—bringing objects from afar;

sentences.zh: 有新必薦，順時令也。

translations.literal: Whenever there is something new it must be offered—following the seasonal order.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever something new appears it must be offered—in accord with the seasons.

sentences.zh: 苑囿之內，躬稼所收，蒐狩之時，親發所中，莫不割鮮擇美，薦而後食，盡誠敬也。

translations.literal: Within the park preserves, what the ruler personally harvested; at hunting times, what the ruler personally shot—none fail to be freshly cut and finely chosen, offered before eating—fully expressing sincerity and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Within the park preserves, whatever the ruler personally harvested, and at hunting times, whatever the ruler personally shot—none fail to be freshly cut and finely chosen, offered before being eaten—expressing the utmost sincerity and reverence.

sentences.zh: 若此至矣，復何加焉！

translations.literal: If it has reached this point, what further addition is there!
translations.idiomatic: When matters have reached this point, what further addition could there be!

sentences.zh: 但當申敕有司，祭如神在，無或簡怠，勖增虔誠。

translations.literal: One need only urgently instruct the responsible officials: sacrifice as if the spirit were present—let none be remiss or negligent, and encourage increased devout sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: One need only urgently instruct the responsible officials to sacrifice as if the spirits were present—let none be remiss or negligent, and encourage greater devout sincerity.

sentences.zh: 其進貢珍羞，或時物鮮美，考諸祠典，無有漏落。

translations.literal: As for tribute delicacies offered up, or timely objects fresh and fine—consult the sacrificial canons, and none are missing or omitted.
translations.idiomatic: As for tribute delicacies offered up, or timely foods fresh and fine—consult the sacrificial canons, and nothing is missing or omitted.

sentences.zh: 皆詳名目，編諸甲令，因宜而薦，以類相從。

translations.literal: All are specified in detail by name and catalog, compiled in the primary regulations, offered as appropriate, and arranged according to category.
translations.idiomatic: All are specified in detail by name and catalog, compiled in the primary regulations, offered as appropriate, and arranged by category.

sentences.zh: 則新鮮肥濃，盡在是矣，不必加於籩豆之數也。

translations.literal: Then freshness, fatness, and richness are all within this—there is no need to add to the number of baskets and dou vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Then everything fresh, rich, and succulent is already included—there is no need to add to the number of food baskets and standing cups.

sentences.zh: 至於祭器，隨物所宜。

translations.literal: As for sacrificial vessels, follow what suits each object.
translations.idiomatic: As for sacrificial vessels, each should suit its contents.

sentences.zh: 故太羹，古食也，盛於㽅。

translations.literal: Therefore the grand soup is ancient food, served in a yan vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the grand soup is ancient food, served in a yan vessel.

sentences.zh: 㽅，古器也；

translations.literal: The yan is an ancient vessel;
translations.idiomatic: The yan is an ancient vessel;

sentences.zh: 和羹，時饌也。

translations.literal: Seasoned soup is present-day fare.
translations.idiomatic: Seasoned soup is present-day fare.

sentences.zh: 盛於铏。

translations.literal: Served in a xing vessel.
translations.idiomatic: It is served in a xing vessel.

sentences.zh: 铏，時器也。

translations.literal: The xing is a present-day vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The xing is a present-day vessel.

sentences.zh: 亦有古饌而盛於時器，故毛血盛於盤，玄酒盛於樽。

translations.literal: There are also ancient foods served in present-day vessels—thus hair-and-blood is served on plates, dark wine in wine jars.
translations.idiomatic: There are also ancient foods served in present-day vessels—thus hair-and-blood is served on plates, and dark wine in wine jars.

sentences.zh: 未有薦時饌而追用古器者，由古質而今文，便於事也。

translations.literal: There has never been offering present-day fare while insistently using ancient vessels—from ancient plainness to present refinement, for convenience in practice.
translations.idiomatic: There has never been offering present-day fare while insistently using ancient vessels—from ancient plainness to present refinement, for convenience in practice.

sentences.zh: 雖加籩豆十二，未足以盡天下美物，而措諸清廟，有兼倍之名，近於侈矣！

translations.literal: Even if baskets and dou are increased to twelve, it is not enough to exhaust all fine objects under Heaven—and placing them in the Pure Temple, with a name implying doubled abundance, approaches extravagance!
translations.idiomatic: Even if food baskets and standing cups were increased to twelve, it would not exhaust all fine objects under Heaven—and placing them in the Pure Temple under a name implying doubled abundance approaches extravagance!

sentences.zh: 魯人丹桓宮之楹，又刻其桷，《春秋》書以「非禮」。

translations.literal: The people of Lu painted the pillars of Duke Huan's palace and carved its rafters—the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded this as "contrary to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Lu painted the pillars of Duke Huan's palace and carved its rafters—the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded this as "contrary to ritual."

sentences.zh: 御孫諫曰：「儉，德之恭也；

translations.literal: Yuzsun remonstrated, saying: "Frugality is the reverence of virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Yuzsun remonstrated, saying: "Frugality is the reverence of virtue;

sentences.zh: 侈，惡之大也。

translations.literal: Extravagance is the greatest of evils.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagance is the greatest of evils.

sentences.zh: 先君有恭德，而君納諸惡，無乃不可乎！

translations.literal: Your predecessor had reverent virtue, yet Your Lordship is adopting evil—is this not inadmissible!
translations.idiomatic: Your predecessor had reverent virtue, yet Your Lordship is adopting what is evil—is this not inadmissible!

sentences.zh: 」是不可以越禮而崇侈於宗廟也。

translations.literal: "—One must not overstep ritual and honor extravagance in the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: "—One must not overstep ritual and honor extravagance in the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 又據《漢書·藝文志》：「墨家之流，出於清廟，是以貴儉」。

translations.literal: Also according to the Treatise on Literature in the Book of Han: "The stream of Mohists arose from the Pure Temple—therefore they prize frugality."
translations.idiomatic: Also according to the Treatise on Literature in the Book of Han: "The stream of Mohists arose from the Pure Temple—therefore they prize frugality."

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，清廟之不尚於奢，舊矣。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, that the Pure Temple does not honor extravagance is an old principle.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from this, the Pure Temple's aversion to extravagance is an old principle.

sentences.zh: 太常所請，恐未可行。

translations.literal: The request of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices—I fear it cannot be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The request of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, I fear, cannot be implemented.

sentences.zh: 又按太常奏狀：「今酌獻酒爵，制度全小，僅未一合，執持甚難，不可全依古制，猶望稍須廣大。

translations.literal: Also examining the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' memorial: "The libation and offering wine cups of today—in design altogether small, barely less than one he in capacity, very difficult to hold—cannot fully follow ancient institutions; one still hopes they may be slightly enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: Also examining the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' memorial: "The libation and offering wine cups of today are altogether too small—barely less than one he in capacity and very difficult to hold—so they cannot fully follow ancient institutions; we still hope they may be slightly enlarged.

sentences.zh: 」竊據禮文，有以小爲貴者，獻以爵，貴其小也。

translations.literal: "I privately rely on ritual text: there are cases where smallness is prized—offering with a jue cup, prizing its smallness.
translations.idiomatic: "I privately rely on the ritual texts: there are cases where smallness is prized—offering with a jue cup prizes its smallness.

sentences.zh: 小不及制，敬而非禮，是有司之失其傳也。

translations.literal: Smallness failing to meet regulation—reverent yet contrary to ritual—this is the responsible officials' failure to preserve the transmission.
translations.idiomatic: When smallness fails to meet regulation, it is reverent yet contrary to ritual—this is the responsible officials' failure to preserve the transmission.

sentences.zh: 固可隨失厘正，無待議而後革。

translations.literal: This can certainly be rectified as the error appears—no need to wait for discussion before reform.
translations.idiomatic: This can certainly be rectified as the error appears—there is no need to wait for discussion before reform.

sentences.zh: 然禮失於敬，猶奢而寧儉，非大過也。

translations.literal: Yet when ritual errs on the side of reverence, it is still better to be frugal than extravagant—not a grave fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when ritual errs on the side of reverence, it is still better to be frugal than extravagant—not a grave fault.

sentences.zh: 未知今制，何所依準。

translations.literal: I do not know what the present institutions rely upon as standard.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know what standard the present institutions rely upon.

sentences.zh: 請兼詳令式，據文而行。

translations.literal: I request that the statutes and regulations also be consulted in detail, and that action be taken according to the text.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the statutes and regulations also be consulted in detail and that action be taken according to the text.

sentences.zh: 又按太常奏狀「外祖服請加至大功九月，舅服請加至小功五月，堂姨、堂舅、舅母請加至袒免」者。

translations.literal: Also examining the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' memorial—"Maternal grandfather mourning requested extension to ninth-month greater mourning; maternal uncle mourning requested extension to fifth-month lesser mourning; paternal aunt, paternal uncle, and maternal uncle's wife requested extension to barest headband mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Also examining the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' memorial requesting that mourning for a maternal grandfather be extended to ninth-month greater mourning, mourning for a maternal uncle to fifth-month lesser mourning, and mourning for a paternal aunt, paternal uncle, and maternal uncle's wife to barest headband mourning.

sentences.zh: 竊聞大道既隱，天下爲家，聖人因之，然後制禮。

translations.literal: I have heard that once the Great Way was obscured and all under Heaven became each family's domain, sages followed this condition and then established ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that once the Great Way was obscured and all under Heaven became each family's domain, sages followed this condition and then established ritual.

sentences.zh: 禮教之設，本於正家，家道正而天下定矣！

translations.literal: The establishment of ritual instruction takes correcting the family as its root—when the way of the family is correct, all under Heaven is settled!
translations.idiomatic: The establishment of ritual instruction takes correcting the family as its root—when the way of the family is correct, all under Heaven is settled!

sentences.zh: 正家之道，不可以貳；

translations.literal: The way of correcting the family cannot be duplicated;
translations.idiomatic: The way of correcting the family cannot be duplicated;

sentences.zh: 總一之義，理歸本宗。

translations.literal: The meaning of unified authority—principle returns to the root lineage.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of unified authority—principle returns to the root lineage.

sentences.zh: 所以父以尊崇，母以厭降，豈亡愛敬，宜存倫序。

translations.literal: Therefore the father is honored through elevation, the mother is reduced through descent—not that love and reverence are absent, but that moral order should be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the father is honored through elevation and the mother is reduced through descent—not that love and reverence are absent, but that moral order should be preserved.

sentences.zh: 是以內有齊斬，外服皆緦，尊名所加，不過一等，此先王不易之道。

translations.literal: Therefore within there are qi and zhan mourning, outside all garments are si mourning—titles of honor added exceed not one grade; this is the unchanging Way of former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore within the family there are qi and zhan mourning, while outside all garments are si mourning—titles of honor added exceed not one grade; this is the unchanging Way of former kings.

sentences.zh: 前聖所誌，後賢所傳，其來久矣。

translations.literal: Recorded by earlier sages, transmitted by later worthies—its origin is long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Recorded by earlier sages and transmitted by later worthies, it dates from long ago.

sentences.zh: 昔辛有適伊川，見被髮而祭於野者，曰：「不及百年，此其戎乎！

translations.literal: Formerly when Xinyou went to Yichuan, he saw someone with disheveled hair sacrificing in the wild and said: "In less than a hundred years, will this be the Rong!
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Xinyou went to Yichuan, he saw someone with disheveled hair sacrificing in the wild and said: "In less than a hundred years, will this be the Rong!

sentences.zh: 其禮先亡矣！

translations.literal: Its ritual will have perished first!"
translations.idiomatic: Its ritual will perish first!"

sentences.zh: 」往修新禮，時改舊章，漸廣《渭陽》之恩，不遵洙、泗之典。

translations.literal: "Past generations revised new rituals, altered old statutes according to the times, gradually broadening the affection of Wei Yang, not following the canons of Zhu and Si.
translations.idiomatic: "Past generations revised new rituals and altered old statutes with the times, gradually broadening the affection celebrated in Wei Yang while not following the canons of Zhu and Si.

sentences.zh: 及弘道之後，唐元之間，國命再移於外族矣。

translations.literal: Reaching after the Hongdao era, in the Tang-Yuan interval, the mandate of state twice shifted to foreign peoples.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hongdao era, in the Tanglong interval, the mandate of state twice shifted to foreign peoples.

sentences.zh: 禮亡徵兆，倘或斯見，天人之際，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: The omen of ritual's loss—perhaps this is seen; between Heaven and man—can one not be warned!
translations.idiomatic: The omen of ritual's loss may already be visible; between Heaven and man—can we not be warned!

sentences.zh: 開元初，補闕盧履冰嘗進狀論喪服輕重，敕令僉議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Reminder Lu Lubing once submitted a memorial discussing the weight and lightness of mourning garments; an edict ordered collective deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Reminder Lu Lubing once submitted a memorial discussing the relative severity of mourning garments, and an edict ordered collective deliberation.

sentences.zh: 於時群議紛挐，各安積習，太常禮部奏依舊定。

translations.literal: At the time group discussion was tangled and clamorous; each rested in accumulated custom; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ministry of Rites memorialized to follow the old fixed standards.
translations.idiomatic: At the time discussions were tangled and clamorous; each faction rested in its accumulated customs; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ministry of Rites memorialized to follow the established standards.

sentences.zh: 陛下運稽古之明，特降別敕，一依古禮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty applied the brilliance of examining antiquity; a special separate edict was issued—entirely following ancient ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty applied the brilliance of examining antiquity and specially issued a separate edict, entirely following ancient ritual.

sentences.zh: 事符典故，人知向方，式固宗盟，社稷之福。

translations.literal: Matters accord with classical precedents; people know the direction; thereby the clan bond is strengthened—the fortune of state and altars.
translations.idiomatic: Matters accord with classical precedents, people know the proper direction, the clan bond is thereby strengthened—a blessing for state and altars.

sentences.zh: 更圖異議，竊所未詳。

translations.literal: To further consider divergent opinions—I privately do not comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: To further consider divergent opinions—I privately do not understand the need.

sentences.zh: 時職方郎中韋述、戸部郎中楊伯成、禮部員外郎楊沖昌、監門兵曹劉秩等，亦建議與沔相符。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Bureau of Appointments Wei Shu, Director in the Ministry of Revenue Yang Bocheng, Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites Yang Chongchang, Military Adjutant of the Gate Guard Liu Zhi, and others also submitted proposals matching Mian's.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Director of the Bureau of Appointments Wei Shu, Director in the Ministry of Revenue Yang Bocheng, Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites Yang Chongchang, Military Adjutant of the Gate Guard Liu Zhi, and others also submitted proposals matching Mian's.

sentences.zh: 俄又令中書門下參詳爲定。

translations.literal: Soon also ordered the Secretariat-Chancellery to examine in detail and set the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the throne also ordered the Secretariat-Chancellery to examine the matter in detail and set the standard.

sentences.zh: 於是宗廟之典，籩豆毎座各加至六，親姨、舅爲小功，舅母加緦麻，堂姨至袒免，餘依舊定，乃下制施行焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon for the ancestral temple canon, baskets and dou at each seat were each increased to six; mourning for maternal aunts and uncles became lesser mourning; maternal uncle's wife gained fine-hemp mourning; paternal aunts reached barest headband mourning; the rest followed old fixed standards—then an edict was issued to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon for the ancestral temple canon, food baskets and standing cups at each seat were increased to six; mourning for maternal aunts and uncles was set at lesser mourning; mourning for a maternal uncle's wife was extended to fine-hemp mourning; mourning for paternal aunts was extended to barest headband mourning; the rest followed established standards—and then an edict was issued to implement it.

sentences.zh: 沔既善禮經，朝廷毎有疑議，皆取決焉。

translations.literal: Mian, being skilled in the ritual classics, whenever the court had doubtful discussions, all took decisions from him.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was skilled in the ritual classics, and whenever the court had doubtful discussions, all turned to him for decisions.

sentences.zh: 二十七年卒，時年六十七，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died; at the time age sixty-seven; posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he died at the age of sixty-seven and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 陸南金陸南金，蘇州呉郡人也。

translations.literal: Lu Nanjin—Lu Nanjin was a man of Wu Prefecture, Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Nanjin was a native of Wu Prefecture in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖士季，從同郡顧野王學《左氏傳》，兼通《史記》、《漢書》。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shi Ji studied the Zuo Commentary from Gu Yewang of the same prefecture, and also mastered the Records of the Grand Historian and Book of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shi Ji studied the Zuo Commentary under Gu Yewang of the same prefecture and also mastered the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 隋末，爲越王侗記室兼侍讀。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, served as Secretary and concurrent Lecturer to Prince Yue Yang Tong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, he served as Secretary and concurrent Lecturer to Prince Yue Yang Tong.

sentences.zh: 侗稱制，授著作郎。

translations.literal: When Tong assumed regency, appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Tong assumed regency, Shi Ji was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 時王世充將行篡奪，侗不平之，謂士季曰：「隋有天下，三十餘載，朝廷文武，遂無烈者乎？

translations.literal: At the time Wang Shichong was about to usurp power; Tong was displeased and said to Shi Ji: "Sui held all under Heaven for thirty-plus years—is there truly no man of fierce resolve among the court's civil and military officials?
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Shichong was about to usurp power; Yang Tong was displeased and said to Shi Ji: "The Sui held all under Heaven for more than thirty years—is there truly no man of fierce resolve among the court's civil and military officials?

sentences.zh: 」士季對曰：「見危授命，臣之宿心。

translations.literal: "Shi Ji replied: "Facing danger and giving one's life—this is my long-held resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ji replied: "Facing danger and giving one's life—this has long been my resolve.

sentences.zh: 請因其啟事，便加手刃。

translations.literal: Please, when he presents business at court, let me at once apply the blade with my own hand.
translations.idiomatic: When he next presents business at court, let me strike him down with my own hand.

sentences.zh: 」事頗泄，遂停士季侍讀。

translations.literal: "The matter leaked somewhat; thereupon Shi Ji's lecturing appointment was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter leaked somewhat, and Shi Ji's appointment as lecturer was terminated.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，爲太學博士，兼弘文館學士，尋卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and concurrent Scholar of the Hongwen Institute; soon died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and concurrent Scholar of the Hongwen Institute, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 南金初爲奉禮郎。

translations.literal: Nanjin at first served as Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjin initially served as Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 開元初，太常少卿盧崇道犯罪，流嶺表，逃歸東都。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lu Chongdao committed a crime, was exiled to Lingnan, and fled back to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lu Chongdao committed a crime, was exiled to Lingnan, and fled back to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時南金以母喪在家，崇道事急，假稱吊賓，造南金，言其情，南金哀而納焉。

translations.literal: At the time Nanjin was at home in mourning for his mother; Chongdao's situation was urgent; falsely claiming to be a condolence guest, he went to Nanjin, explained his plight, and Nanjin pitying him took him in.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Nanjin was at home mourning his mother; Chongdao's situation was urgent; posing as a condolence visitor, he went to Nanjin, explained his plight, and Nanjin, pitying him, took him in.

sentences.zh: 崇道俄爲仇人所發，詔使侍御史王旭按其事，遂捕獲崇道，連引南金，旭遂繩以重法。

translations.literal: Before long Chongdao was exposed by an enemy; an edict sent Investigating Censor Wang Xu to investigate the matter; thereby Chongdao was captured and Nanjin was implicated; Xu then applied severe law.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chongdao was exposed by an enemy; an edict sent Investigating Censor Wang Xu to investigate; Chongdao was captured and Nanjin was implicated, and Xu applied the severest penalties.

sentences.zh: 南金弟 趙璧南金弟趙璧詣旭，自言藏崇道，請代兄死。

translations.literal: Nanjin's younger brother Zhao Bi—Nanjin's younger brother Zhao Bi went to Xu, confessing he had hidden Chongdao, requesting to die in his brother's stead.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjin's younger brother Zhao Bi went to Xu, confessing that he had hidden Chongdao and asking to die in his brother's stead.

sentences.zh: 南金固稱：「弟實自誣，身請當罪。

translations.literal: Nanjin firmly declared: "My brother has in truth falsely accused himself; I request to bear the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjin firmly declared: "My brother has in truth falsely accused himself; let me bear the crime.

sentences.zh: 」兄弟讓死，旭怪而問其故。

translations.literal: "The brothers contended over who should die; Xu marveled and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers each claimed death for the other; Xu marveled and asked why.

sentences.zh: 趙璧曰：「兄是長嫡，又能幹家事。

translations.literal: Zhao Bi said: "My elder brother is the eldest legitimate son and can manage household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bi said: "My elder brother is the eldest legitimate son and can manage household affairs.

sentences.zh: 亡母未葬，小妹未嫁，自惟幼劣，生無所益，身自請死。

translations.literal: Our deceased mother is not yet buried; our little sister is not yet married; considering myself young and inferior, of no benefit in life—I personally request death.
translations.idiomatic: Our deceased mother is not yet buried; our little sister is not yet married; considering myself young and of little use, I personally ask to die.

sentences.zh: 」旭遂列上狀，上嘉其友義，並特宥之。

translations.literal: "Xu thereupon submitted a memorial detailing the matter; the throne praised their bonds of friendship and specially pardoned them both.
translations.idiomatic: Xu thereupon submitted a memorial detailing the matter; the throne praised their bonds of friendship and specially pardoned them both.

sentences.zh: 南金由是大知名。

translations.literal: Nanjin thereby became greatly renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjin thereby became greatly renowned.

sentences.zh: 南金頗涉經史，言行修謹，左丞相張説及宗人太子少保象先，皆欽重之。

translations.literal: Nanjin was broadly versed in classics and histories; conduct and speech were cultivated and careful; Left Chancellor Zhang Yue and clansman Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Xiang Xian all held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjin was broadly versed in the classics and histories, his conduct and speech cultivated and careful; Left Chancellor Zhang Yue and his clansman Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Xiang Xian all held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 累轉庫部員外郎，以疾，固辭不堪繁劇，轉爲太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Successively transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; due to illness, firmly declined being unable to bear heavy duties; transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, but due to illness firmly declined the demanding duties and was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十餘。

translations.literal: Died, age fifty-plus.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his fifties.

sentences.zh: 張琇張琇者，蒲州解人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiu—Zhang Xiu was a man of Jie in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu was a native of Jie in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父審素，爲巂州都督，在邊累載。

translations.literal: His father Shen Su was Military Commissioner of Xi Prefecture, at the frontier many years.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen Su was Military Commissioner of Xi Prefecture and served on the frontier for many years.

sentences.zh: 俄有糾其軍中贓罪，敕監察御史楊汪馳傳就軍按之。

translations.literal: Soon someone impeached him for embezzlement in the army; an edict sent Investigating Censor Yang Wang by fast relay to the army to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone impeached him for embezzlement in the army; an edict sent Investigating Censor Yang Wang by fast relay to the army to investigate.

sentences.zh: 汪在路，爲審素黨與所劫，對汪殺告事者，脅汪令奏雪審素之罪。

translations.literal: Wang was on the road when Shen Su's partisan associates seized him; in Wang's presence they killed the accuser and coerced Wang to memorialize clearing Shen Su's crime.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang was still en route, Shen Su's partisan associates seized him; in Wang's presence they killed the accuser and coerced Wang into memorializing to clear Shen Su's crime.

sentences.zh: 俄而州人翻殺審素之黨，汪始得還。

translations.literal: Before long the people of the prefecture in turn killed Shen Su's partisans; Wang was then able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the people of the prefecture in turn killed Shen Su's partisans, and Wang was then able to return.

sentences.zh: 至益州，奏稱審素謀反，因深按審素，構成其罪。

translations.literal: Reaching Yi Prefecture, he memorialized claiming Shen Su plotted rebellion; thereby deeply investigating Shen Su and framing his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yi Prefecture, he memorialized claiming that Shen Su had plotted rebellion, deeply investigated him, and framed him for the crime.

sentences.zh: 斬之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Executed him and confiscated his household property.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Su was executed and his household property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 琇與兄瑝，以年幼坐徙嶺外。

translations.literal: Xiu and elder brother Huang, due to youth, were sentenced to exile beyond the Ling passes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and his elder brother Huang, because they were young, were sentenced to exile beyond the Ling passes.

sentences.zh: 尋各逃歸，累年隱匿。

translations.literal: Soon each fled back home; for years concealed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Soon each fled home and lived in hiding for years.

sentences.zh: 汪後累轉殿中侍御史，改名萬頃。

translations.literal: Later Wang was successively transferred to Palace Investigating Censor; changed name to Wan Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was subsequently promoted to Palace Investigating Censor and changed his name to Wan Qing.

sentences.zh: ，瑝、琇候萬頃於都城，挺刃殺之。

translations.literal: Huang and Xiu waited for Wan Qing in the capital; drew blades and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang and Xiu waited for Wan Qing in the capital, drew their blades, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 瑝雖年長，其發謀及手刃，皆琇爲之。

translations.literal: Although Huang was older, the plotting and the hand that struck the blow were both Xiu's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Although Huang was older, Xiu had done all the plotting and had struck the blow himself.

sentences.zh: 既殺萬頃，系表於斧刃，自言報仇之狀。

translations.literal: Having killed Wan Qing, tied a memorial to the axe blade, stating themselves the circumstances of vengeance.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Wan Qing, they tied a written statement to the axe blade explaining the circumstances of their vengeance.

sentences.zh: 便逃奔，將就江外，殺與萬頃同謀構父罪者。

translations.literal: At once fled; intending to go to the region beyond the Yangzi, kill those who with Wan Qing conspired to frame their father's crime.
translations.idiomatic: They fled at once, intending to go to the region south of the Yangzi and kill those who had conspired with Wan Qing to frame their father.

sentences.zh: 行至汜水，爲捕者所獲。

translations.literal: Reaching Sishui, were seized by pursuers.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Sishui, they were seized by pursuers.

sentences.zh: 時都城士女，皆矜琇等幼稚孝烈，能復父仇，多言其合矜恕者。

translations.literal: At the time the men and women of the capital all admired Xiu and the others' youthful filial heroism, able to avenge their father; many said they deserved clemency.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the men and women of the capital all admired Xiu and the others for their youthful filial heroism in avenging their father, and many said they deserved clemency.

sentences.zh: 中書令張九齡又欲活之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling again wished to spare their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling again wished to spare their lives.

sentences.zh: 裴耀卿、李林甫固言：「國法不可縱報仇。

translations.literal: Pei Yaoqing and Li Linfu firmly argued: "State law cannot permit revenge killings to go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoqing and Li Linfu firmly argued: "State law cannot permit revenge killings to go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 」上以爲然，因謂九齡等曰：「復仇雖禮法所許，殺人亦格律具存。

translations.literal: "The emperor agreed and therefore said to Jiuling and the others: "Though revenge is permitted by ritual and law, the statutes for homicide remain fully in force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and said to Jiuling and the others: "Though revenge is permitted by ritual and law, the statutes governing homicide remain fully in force.

sentences.zh: 孝子之情，義不顧命，國家設法，焉得容此！

translations.literal: The heart of a filial son, bound by duty, does not consider his life—but when the state establishes laws, how can it tolerate this!
translations.idiomatic: The heart of a filial son, bound by duty, does not consider his own life—but when the state establishes laws, how can it tolerate this!

sentences.zh: 殺之成復仇之志，赦之虧律格之條。

translations.literal: To execute them fulfills the wish for vengeance; to pardon them violates the articles of the legal codes.
translations.idiomatic: To execute them would fulfill their wish for vengeance; to pardon them would violate the articles of the legal codes.

sentences.zh: 然道路誼議，故須告示。

translations.literal: Yet there is public sentiment along the roads, so a proclamation is needed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there is much public sentiment, so a proclamation is needed.

sentences.zh: 」乃下敕曰：「張瑝等兄弟同殺，推問款承。

translations.literal: "He thereupon issued an edict saying: "Zhang Huang and his brothers jointly committed murder; upon interrogation they confessed fully.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon issued an edict saying: "Zhang Huang and his brothers jointly committed murder; upon interrogation they confessed fully.

sentences.zh: 律有正條，俱各至死。

translations.literal: The law has explicit articles; each is liable to death.
translations.idiomatic: The law has explicit articles; each is liable to death.

sentences.zh: 近聞士庶，頗有誼詞，矜其爲父復仇，或言本罪冤濫。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard that among officials and commoners there is much sympathetic talk, praising them for avenging their father, or saying the original conviction was unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have heard that among officials and commoners there is much sympathetic talk, praising them for avenging their father or saying the original conviction was unjust.

sentences.zh: 但國家設法，事在經久，蓋以濟人，期於止殺。

translations.literal: But when the state establishes laws, the aim is permanence—it is meant to aid people and to stop killing.
translations.idiomatic: But when the state establishes laws, the aim is permanence—it is meant to aid people and to stop killing.

sentences.zh: 各申爲子之志，誰非徇孝之夫，展轉相繼，相殺何限！

translations.literal: If each can assert a son's resolve, who is not a man devoted to filial duty? Passed from hand to hand in succession—how limitless would mutual killing become!
translations.idiomatic: If each can assert a son's resolve, who is not a man devoted to filial duty? Passed from hand to hand in succession—how limitless would mutual killing become!

sentences.zh: 咎由作士，法在必行；

translations.literal: Blame lies with those who first made the law; the law must be enforced;
translations.idiomatic: Blame lies with those who first made the law; the law must be enforced;

sentences.zh: 曾參殺人，亦不可恕。

translations.literal: even Zeng Shen's killing a man could not be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: even if Zeng Shen had killed a man, it could not be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 不能加以刑戮，肆諸市朝，宜付河南府告示決殺。

translations.literal: Though I cannot have them punished by execution in the market and court, they should be handed to Henan Prefecture to be proclaimed and executed by sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Though I cannot have them executed publicly in the market and court, they should be handed to Henan Prefecture to be proclaimed and executed by sentence.

sentences.zh: 瑝、琇既死，士庶咸傷湣之，爲作哀誄，榜於衢路。

translations.literal: When Huang and Xiu had died, officials and commoners all mourned them deeply; people wrote elegies and posted them at crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang and Xiu had died, officials and commoners all mourned them deeply; people wrote elegies and posted them at crossroads.

sentences.zh: 市人斂錢，於死所造義井，並葬瑝、琇於北邙。

translations.literal: Townspeople collected money, built a public well at the place of death, and together buried Huang and Xiu on North Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Townspeople collected money, built a public well at the place of death, and together buried Huang and Xiu on North Mang.

sentences.zh: 又恐萬頃家人發之，并作疑塚數所。

translations.literal: Fearing Wan Qing's family might disinter them, they also built several decoy tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Wan Qing's family might disinter them, they also built several decoy tombs.

sentences.zh: 其爲時人所傷如此。

translations.literal: Such was the depth of public grief for them.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of public grief for them.

sentences.zh: 梁文貞梁文貞，虢州閿鄕人。

translations.literal: Liang Wenzhen—Liang Wenzhen was a native of Wenxiang in Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wenzhen was a native of Wenxiang in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少從徵役，比回而父母皆卒。

translations.literal: In youth he followed conscript service; by the time he returned, both parents had died.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he followed conscript service; by the time he returned, both parents had died.

sentences.zh: 文貞恨不獲終養，乃穿壙爲門，磴道出入，晨夕灑掃其中。

translations.literal: Wenzhen grieved that he had been unable to care for them to the end; he therefore cut a door in the burial chamber, made a stepped path for entry and exit, and morning and evening swept and cleaned inside.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen grieved that he had been unable to care for them to the end; he cut a door in the burial chamber, made a stepped path for entry and exit, and morning and evening swept and cleaned inside.

sentences.zh: 結廬墓側，未嘗暫離。

translations.literal: He built a hut beside the tomb and never left even briefly.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut beside the tomb and never left even briefly.

sentences.zh: 自是不言三十年，家人有所問，但畫字以對。

translations.literal: From then on he did not speak for thirty years; when family asked him anything, he only wrote characters in reply.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he did not speak for thirty years; when family asked him anything, he only wrote characters in reply.

sentences.zh: 其後山水沖斷驛路，更於原上開道，經文貞墓前。

translations.literal: Later, floods and landslides cut off the post road; a new route was opened on the plain, passing before Wenzhen's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Later floods and landslides cut off the post road; a new route was opened on the plain, passing before Wenzhen's tomb.

sentences.zh: 由是行旅見之，遠近莫不欽嘆。

translations.literal: Travelers thereby saw him; near and far, none failed to admire and marvel.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers thereby saw him; near and far, all admired and marveled.

sentences.zh: 有甘露降塋前樹，白兔馴擾，鄕人以爲孝感所致。

translations.literal: Sweet dew descended on the tree before the grave mound; a white rabbit came tamely about; villagers took it as brought on by filial devotion moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet dew descended on the tree before the grave mound; a white rabbit came tamely about; villagers believed it was brought on by filial devotion moving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 開元初，縣令崔季友刊石以紀之。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era, Magistrate Cui Jiyou carved a stone to record it.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan era, Magistrate Cui Jiyou carved a stone to record it.

sentences.zh: 十四年，刺史許景先奏：「文貞孝行絶倫，泣血廬墓，三十餘年，請宣付史官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Prefect Xu Jingxian memorialized: "Wenzhen's filial conduct is without peer; weeping blood he dwelt by the tomb more than thirty years—I request this be proclaimed and handed to the historians.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Prefect Xu Jingxian memorialized: "Wenzhen's filial conduct is without peer; weeping blood he dwelt by the tomb for more than thirty years—I request this be proclaimed and handed to the historians.

sentences.zh: 」是歳，御史大夫崔隱甫廷奏：「恆州鹿泉人李處恭、張義貞兩家，祖父自國初已來，異姓同居，至今三代，百有餘年。

translations.literal: "That year, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yinfu presented at court: "The households of Li Chugong and Zhang Yizhen of Luquan in Heng Prefecture—from their grandfathers since the founding of the dynasty, different surnames have lived together; to now three generations, more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yinfu presented at court: "The households of Li Chugong and Zhang Yizhen of Luquan in Heng Prefecture—from their grandfathers since the founding of the dynasty, different surnames have lived together; to now three generations, more than a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 又青州北海人呂元簡，四代同居，至所畜牛馬羊狗，皆異母共乳。

translations.literal: Also Lü Yuanjian of Beihai in Qing Prefecture—four generations living together; even the cattle, horses, sheep, and dogs they kept all nursed from different mothers together.
translations.idiomatic: Also Lü Yuanjian of Beihai in Qing Prefecture—four generations living together; even the cattle, horses, sheep, and dogs they kept all nursed from different mothers together.

sentences.zh: 請加旌表，仍編入史館。

translations.literal: I request they be granted commemorative honors and entered in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: I request they be granted commemorative honors and entered in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 」制皆許之。

translations.literal: "Edicts approved all.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts approved all.

sentences.zh: 崔衍崔衍，左丞倫之子。

translations.literal: Cui Yan—Cui Yan was son of Vice Director Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan was the son of Vice Director Lun.

sentences.zh: 繼母李氏，不慈於衍。

translations.literal: His stepmother Lady Li was unkind toward Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother Lady Li was unkind toward Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍時爲富平尉，倫使於吐蕃，久方歸，李氏衣弊衣以見倫。

translations.literal: Yan was then Marshal of Fuping; Lun had been sent as envoy to Tibet and only after long absence returned; Lady Li wore shabby clothes to meet Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was then Marshal of Fuping; Lun had been sent as envoy to Tibet and only after a long absence returned; Lady Li wore shabby clothes to meet Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫問其故，李氏稱：「自倫使於蕃中，衍不給衣食。

translations.literal: Lun asked the reason; Lady Li claimed: "Since Lun went as envoy among the Tibetans, Yan has not supplied food or clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Lun asked the reason; Lady Li claimed: "Since Lun went as envoy among the Tibetans, Yan has not supplied food or clothing.

sentences.zh: 」倫大怒，召衍責詬，命僕隸拉於地，袒其背，將鞭之。

translations.literal: "Lun flew into rage, summoned Yan and reviled him, ordered servants to pull him to the ground, bared his back, and was about to flog him.
translations.idiomatic: Lun flew into a rage, summoned Yan and reviled him, ordered servants to pull him to the ground, bared his back, and was about to flog him.

sentences.zh: 衍涕泣，終不自陳。

translations.literal: Yan wept but to the end did not plead his own case.
translations.idiomatic: Yan wept but to the end did not plead his own case.

sentences.zh: 倫弟殷，聞之趨往，以身蔽衍，杖不得下。

translations.literal: Lun's younger brother Yin, hearing of it, rushed there and shielded Yan with his body so the staff could not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's younger brother Yin, hearing of it, rushed there and shielded Yan with his body so the staff could not fall.

sentences.zh: 因大言曰：「衍毎月俸錢，皆送嫂處，殷所具知，何忍乃言衍不給衣食！

translations.literal: He then cried out: "Yan every month sends his salary to our sister-in-law—Yin knows this fully—how can you bear to say Yan does not supply food and clothing!
translations.idiomatic: He then cried out: "Yan every month sends his salary to our sister-in-law—Yin knows this fully—how can you bear to say Yan does not supply food and clothing!

sentences.zh: 」倫怒乃解。

translations.literal: "Lun's anger then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's anger then subsided.

sentences.zh: 由是倫遂不聽李氏之譖。

translations.literal: Thereby Lun ceased to heed Lady Li's slanders.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby Lun ceased to heed Lady Li's slanders.

sentences.zh: 及倫卒，衍事李氏益謹。

translations.literal: When Lun died, Yan served Lady Li all the more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun died, Yan served Lady Li all the more carefully.

sentences.zh: 李氏所生子郃，毎多取子母錢，使其主以契書徵負于衍。

translations.literal: He, the son Lady Li bore, often took much money lent on interest and had his agent collect debts from Yan with contracts.
translations.idiomatic: He, the son Lady Li bore, often took large sums lent on interest and had his agent collect debts from Yan with written contracts.

sentences.zh: 衍歳爲償之，故衍官至江州刺史，而妻子衣食無所餘。

translations.literal: Yan repaid year by year, so though Yan reached the post of Prefect of Jiangzhou, his wife and children had nothing left for food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan repaid year by year, so though he rose to Prefect of Jiangzhou, his wife and children had nothing left for food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 後歷蘇、虢二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Prefect of Su and Guo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served successively as Prefect of Su and Guo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 虢居陜、華二州之間，而稅重數倍。

translations.literal: Guo lay between Shaan and Hua prefectures, yet its taxes were many times heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Guo lay between Shaan and Hua prefectures, yet its taxes were many times heavier.

sentences.zh: 其青苗錢，華、陜之郊，畝出十有八；

translations.literal: For green-sprout tax, in the outskirts of Hua and Shaan, eighteen per mu were levied;
translations.idiomatic: For the green-sprout tax, in the outskirts of Hua and Shaan eighteen per mu were levied;

sentences.zh: 而虢之郊，毎徵十之七。

translations.literal: but in the outskirts of Guo, seven tenths were collected each time.
translations.idiomatic: but in the outskirts of Guo seven tenths were collected each time.

sentences.zh: 衍乃上其事。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yan thereupon memorialized the matter.

sentences.zh: 時裴延齡領度支，方務聚斂，乃紿衍以前後刺史無言者。

translations.literal: At the time Pei Yanling headed the Revenue Bureau and was busy with accumulation; he deceived Yan saying no previous prefect had spoken of it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Pei Yanling headed the Revenue Bureau and was busy with accumulation; he deceived Yan by saying no previous prefect had spoken of it.

sentences.zh: 衍又上陳人困，曰：「臣所治多是山田，且當郵傳沖要，屬歳不登，頗甚流離。

translations.literal: Yan again memorialized reporting people's hardship, saying: "The districts I govern are mostly mountain fields, and moreover lie on vital post-road routes; as harvests have failed, displacement is severe.
translations.idiomatic: Yan again memorialized reporting the people's hardship, saying: "The districts I govern are mostly mountain fields, and moreover lie on vital post-road routes; as harvests have failed, displacement is severe.

sentences.zh: 舊額賦租，特望蠲減。

translations.literal: The established tax quotas—I especially hope for remission and reduction.
translations.idiomatic: The established tax quotas—I especially hope for remission and reduction.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見比來諸郡論百姓間事，患在長吏因循不爲申請，不詣實，不患朝廷不矜放。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that in recent times when prefectures discuss matters among the common people, the trouble lies in senior officials dragging their feet and not petitioning—not in lack of truth, not in fear that the court will not show compassion and remit.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant observes that in recent times when prefectures discuss matters affecting the common people, the trouble lies in senior officials dragging their feet and not petitioning—not in lack of truth, not in fear that the court will not show compassion and remit.

sentences.zh: 有以不言受譴者，未有言而獲罪者。

translations.literal: There are cases of punishment for remaining silent; there are none of punishment for speaking.
translations.idiomatic: There are cases of punishment for remaining silent; there are none of punishment for speaking.

sentences.zh: 陛下拔臣牧大郡，委臣撫疲民，臣所以不敢顧望，茍求自安，敢罄狂瞽，上干聖覽。

translations.literal: Your Majesty promoted me to govern a great prefecture and charged me to comfort weary people; therefore I dare not look back in hesitation or seek my own ease—I dare exhaust my reckless blindness and disturb Your Sagely gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty promoted me to govern a great prefecture and charged me to comfort weary people; therefore I dare not look back in hesitation or seek my own ease—I dare exhaust my reckless blindness and disturb Your Sagely gaze.

sentences.zh: 」帝以衍詞理切直，乃特敕度支，令減虢州青苗錢。

translations.literal: "The emperor, finding Yan's language trenchant and straight, specially ordered the Revenue Bureau to reduce Guo Prefecture's green-sprout tax.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding Yan's language trenchant and straight, specially ordered the Revenue Bureau to reduce Guo Prefecture's green-sprout tax.

sentences.zh: 遷宣歙池觀察使，政務簡便，人頗懷之。

translations.literal: Transferred to Military Commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi—administration was simple and convenient; people greatly cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi; his administration was simple and convenient, and the people greatly cherished him.

sentences.zh: 其所擇從事，多得名流。

translations.literal: Those he chose as staff members were mostly men of renown.
translations.idiomatic: Those he chose as staff members were mostly men of renown.

sentences.zh: 時有位者待賓僚率輕傲，衍獨加禮敬，幕中之士，後多顯達。

translations.literal: At the time officeholders generally treated guests and staff with casual disdain; Yan alone showed them honor and respect; men in his staff later mostly rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time officeholders generally treated guests and staff with casual disdain; Yan alone showed them honor and respect, and men in his staff later mostly rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，天下好進奉以結主恩，徵求聚斂，州郡耗竭，韋臯、劉贊、裴肅爲之首。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, throughout the realm people favored presenting tribute to win imperial favor; exactions and accumulation exhausted prefectures and commanderies—Wei Gao, Liu Zan, and Pei Su led the way.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era, throughout the realm people favored presenting tribute to win imperial favor; exactions and accumulation exhausted prefectures and commanderies—Wei Gao, Liu Zan, and Pei Su led the way.

sentences.zh: 贊死而衍代其位。

translations.literal: When Zan died, Yan replaced him in the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zan died, Yan replaced him in the post.

sentences.zh: 衍雖不能驟革其弊，居宣州十年，頗勤儉，府庫盈溢。

translations.literal: Though Yan could not swiftly reform these abuses, during ten years at Xuanzhou he was quite frugal and industrious, and the treasury overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yan could not swiftly reform these abuses, during ten years at Xuanzhou he was quite frugal and industrious, and the treasury overflowed.

sentences.zh: 及穆贊代衍，宣州歳饉，遂以錢四十二萬貫代百姓稅，故宣州人不至流散。

translations.literal: When Mu Zan replaced Yan, Xuanzhou suffered famine that year; he then used 420,000 strings of cash to pay taxes on behalf of the people, so the people of Xuanzhou did not scatter in flight.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu Zan replaced Yan, Xuanzhou suffered famine that year; he used 420,000 strings of cash to pay taxes on behalf of the people, so the people of Xuanzhou did not scatter in flight.

sentences.zh: ，詔加工部尚書。

translations.literal: An edict added the title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added the title Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 丁公著丁公著，字平子，蘇州呉郡人。

translations.literal: Ding Gongzhu—Ding Gongzhu, styled Pingzi, was a native of Wu Commandery in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Gongzhu, styled Pingzi, was a native of Wu Commandery in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖衷，父緒，皆不仕。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhong and father Xu both did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhong and father Xu both did not take office.

sentences.zh: 公著生三歳，喪所親。

translations.literal: Gongzhu lost a close relative at age three.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu lost a close relative at age three.

sentences.zh: 七歳，見鄰母抱其子，哀感不食，因請於父，絶粒奉道，冀其幽贊，父憫而從之。

translations.literal: At seven, seeing a neighbor's mother holding her child, he was moved to grief and would not eat; he then asked his father, abstaining from grain to follow the Way in hope of spiritual aid; his father pitying him consented.
translations.idiomatic: At seven, seeing a neighbor's mother holding her child, he was moved to grief and would not eat; he asked his father to let him abstain from grain and follow the Way in hope of spiritual aid, and his father, pitying him, consented.

sentences.zh: 年十七，父勉令就學。

translations.literal: At seventeen his father urged him to begin study.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen his father urged him to begin his studies.

sentences.zh: 年二十一，《五經》及第。

translations.literal: At twenty-one he passed the Five Classics examination.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-one he passed the Five Classics examination.

sentences.zh: 明年，又通《開元禮》，授集賢校書郎。

translations.literal: The next year he also passed the Kaiyuan Rites examination and was appointed Collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he also passed the Kaiyuan Rites examination and was appointed Collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 秩未終，歸侍鄕里，不應請辟。

translations.literal: Before his term ended he returned home to serve in his village and did not respond to invitations to office.
translations.idiomatic: Before his term ended he returned home to serve in his village and did not respond to invitations to office.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，躬負土成墳，哀毀之容，人爲憂之，里閭聞風，皆敦孝悌。

translations.literal: During mourning for his father he personally carried earth to complete the mound; his grief-wasted appearance made people worry for him; hearing of it, the neighborhood all practiced filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he personally carried earth to complete the mound; his grief-wasted appearance made people worry for him; hearing of it, the whole neighborhood practiced filial piety and brotherly respect.

sentences.zh: 觀察使薛華表其行，詔賜粟帛，旌其門閭。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Xue Hua memorialized his conduct; an edict bestowed grain and silk and honored his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner Xue Hua memorialized his conduct; an edict bestowed grain and silk and honored his gate and lane.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使李吉甫慕其才行，薦授太子文學，兼集賢殿校理。

translations.literal: Huainan Military Commissioner Li Jifu admired his character and ability and recommended him as Literary Attendant to the Heir Apparent, also Collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan Military Commissioner Li Jifu admired his character and ability and recommended him as Literary Attendant to the Heir Apparent, also serving as Collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 吉甫自淮南入相，廷薦其行，即日授右補闕。

translations.literal: Jifu entering the capital from Huainan as chancellor, recommended his conduct at court; that same day he was appointed Remonstrator on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu entered the capital from Huainan as chancellor, he recommended Gongzhu's conduct at court; that same day Gongzhu was appointed Remonstrator on the Right.

sentences.zh: 遷集賢直學士，尋授水部員外郎，充皇太子及諸王侍讀。

translations.literal: Promoted to Academician-in-Attendance at the Hall of Assembled Worthies; soon appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works' Water Bureau, serving as Reader to the Crown Prince and the princes.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician-in-Attendance at the Hall of Assembled Worthies; soon appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works' Water Bureau, serving as Reader to the Crown Prince and the princes.

sentences.zh: 著《皇太子及諸王訓》十卷。

translations.literal: Authored ten scrolls of Instructions for the Crown Prince and the Princes.
translations.idiomatic: He authored ten scrolls of Instructions for the Crown Prince and the Princes.

sentences.zh: 轉駕部員外，仍兼舊職。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works' Chariot Bureau, still holding his former duties concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works' Chariot Bureau, still holding his former duties concurrently.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，未及聽政，召居禁中，詢訪朝典，以宰相許之。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, before he had yet attended to governance, Gongzhu was summoned to dwell in the inner palace, consulted on court precedents, and promised the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong ascended the throne, before he had yet attended to governance, Gongzhu was summoned to dwell in the inner palace, consulted on court precedents, and promised the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 公著陳情，詞意極切，超授給事中，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: Gongzhu stated his feelings; his language was extremely earnest; he was specially appointed Controller of Briefs and given the purple-gold fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu stated his feelings in language that was extremely earnest; he was specially appointed Controller of Briefs and given the purple-gold fish tally.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷工部侍郎，仍兼集賢殿學士，寵青宮之舊也。

translations.literal: Before long promoted to Vice Minister of Works, still concurrently Academician at the Hall of Assembled Worthies—favor for his old ties in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works, still concurrently Academician at the Hall of Assembled Worthies—favor for his old ties in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 知吏部選事。

translations.literal: He oversaw selection matters in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw selection matters in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 公著知將欲大用，以疾辭退，因求外官，遂授浙江西道都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: Gongzhu knew they intended great promotion; citing illness he declined and sought an outer post; he was therefore appointed Military Commissioner of all Zhejiang West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu knew they intended to promote him greatly; citing illness he declined and sought an outer post; he was therefore appointed Military Commissioner of all Zhejiang West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二年，授河南尹。

translations.literal: In the second year appointed Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 皆以清靜爲理。

translations.literal: In all cases he governed through quiet simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases he governed through quiet simplicity.

sentences.zh: 改尚書右丞，轉兵部、吏部侍郎，遷禮部尚書、翰林侍講學士。
