translations.literal: Changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; transferred to Vice Minister of War and Vice Minister of Personnel; promoted to Minister of Rites and Lecturing Academician of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; transferred to Vice Minister of War and Vice Minister of Personnel; promoted to Minister of Rites and Lecturing Academician of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 上以浙西災寇，詢求良帥，命檢校戸部尚書領之。

translations.literal: The emperor, with disaster and banditry in Zhexi, sought a worthy commander and ordered him as Acting Minister of Revenue to lead the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, with disaster and banditry in Zhexi, sought a worthy commander and ordered him as Acting Minister of Revenue to lead the circuit.

sentences.zh: 詔賜米七萬碩以賑給，浙民賴之。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed seventy thousand hu of grain for relief; the people of Zhe relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict bestowed seventy thousand hu of grain for relief; the people of Zhe relied on it.

sentences.zh: 改授太常卿，以疾請歸鄕里，未至而終，年六十四。

translations.literal: Reassigned as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; citing illness he requested return home; before arriving he died, age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; citing illness he requested return home; before arriving he died, age sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈右僕射，廢朝一日。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Right Vice Director; court mourning was suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director; court mourning was suspended for one day.

sentences.zh: 著《禮志》十卷。

translations.literal: He authored ten fascicles of the Treatise on Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ten fascicles of a Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 公著清儉守道，毎得一官，未嘗不憂色滿容。

translations.literal: Gongzhu was pure, frugal, and upheld the Way; whenever he received an office he never failed to show a face full of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu was pure, frugal, and steadfast in the Way; whenever he received a new appointment, his face was always clouded with worry.

sentences.zh: 年四十四喪室，以至終身，無妓妾聲樂之好。

translations.literal: At forty-four he lost his wife; to the end of his life he had no fondness for concubines or music.
translations.idiomatic: When he was forty-four his wife died, and for the rest of his life he took no pleasure in concubines or music.

sentences.zh: 兇問至日，中外痛惜之。

translations.literal: On the day the grievous news arrived, within and without the court all grieved and regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived, the court and the people alike mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 羅讓羅讓，字景宣。

translations.literal: Luo Rang—Luo Rang, styled Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Rang, styled Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 祖懷操。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Huaicao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Luo Huaicao.

sentences.zh: 父珦，官至京兆尹。

translations.literal: His father Bang reached the office of metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luo Bang rose to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 讓少以文學知名，舉進士，應詔對策高等，爲咸陽尉。

translations.literal: Rang was famed in youth for literary accomplishment; he passed the jinshi examination, responded to the imperial decree examination with high rank, and became magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rang was known in youth for literary talent; he passed the jinshi examination, earned a high grade in the imperial decree examination, and became magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，尚衣麻茹菜，不從四方之辟者十餘年。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning; when mourning ended he still wore hemp and ate coarse vegetables, not accepting invitations from the four directions for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he completed mourning but continued to wear hemp and eat plain food, refusing appointments from all quarters for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 李獻爲淮南節度使，就其所居，請爲從事。

translations.literal: Li Xian was military governor of Huainan; he came to Rang's residence and invited him to serve on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, military governor of Huainan, came to his home and invited him to join his staff.

sentences.zh: 除監察御史，轉殿中，歷尚書郎、給事中，累遷至福建觀察使、兼御史中丞，甚著仁惠。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor, transferred to the palace bureau, served as secretariat director and attendant censor, and was repeatedly promoted to military commissioner of Fujian and concurrently vice censor-in-chief, greatly renowned for kindness and grace.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor, then transferred to the palace bureau, served as a secretariat director and attendant censor, and rose to military commissioner of Fujian with the concurrent title of vice censor-in-chief, winning renown for benevolent governance.

sentences.zh: 有以女奴遺讓者，讓問其所因，曰：「本某寺家人。

translations.literal: Someone presented him with a female slave; Rang asked how this had come about; she said: 'Originally I was a household person of a certain monastery.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone gave him a female slave; when Rang asked how she had come to be sold, she replied, "I was originally a dependent of a monastery."

sentences.zh: 兄姊九人，皆爲官所賣，其留者唯老母耳。

translations.literal: Nine elder and younger siblings were all sold by officials; the one who remained was only my old mother.
translations.idiomatic: Nine brothers and sisters were all sold off by the authorities; only my aged mother was left behind.

sentences.zh: 」讓慘然，焚其券書，以女奴歸其母。

translations.literal: Rang was deeply moved, burned the bond, and returned the female slave to her mother.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, Rang burned the contract and sent the girl back to her mother.

sentences.zh: 入爲散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He entered court as supernumerary palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court as supernumerary palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除江西都團練觀察使、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed military commissioner of Jiangxi and concurrently chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed military commissioner of Jiangxi with the concurrent title of chief censor.

sentences.zh: 年七十一卒。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 讓子 劭京子劭京，字子峻，進士擢第，又登科。

translations.literal: Rang's son Zhaojing—Zhaojing, styled Zijun, passed the jinshi examination and also passed a special examination.
translations.idiomatic: Rang's son Luo Zhaojing, styled Zijun, passed the jinshi examination and also passed a special examination.

sentences.zh: 讓再從弟詠。

translations.literal: Rang's second cousin once removed was Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Rang's second cousin once removed was Luo Yong.

sentences.zh: 詠子劭權，字昭衡，進士擢第。

translations.literal: Yong's son Shaoquan, styled Zhaoheng, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's son Luo Shaoquan, styled Zhaoheng, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 劭京、劭權知名於時，並歷清貫。

translations.literal: Zhaojing and Shaoquan were famed in their time and both held pure, high offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojing and Shaoquan were celebrated in their day and both rose through the ranks of pure, high office.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：麒麟鳳凰，飛走之類。

translations.literal: Commentary says: The qilin and phoenix belong to the class of flying and running creatures.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The qilin and phoenix belong among creatures that fly and run.

sentences.zh: 唯孝與悌，亦爲人瑞。

translations.literal: Only filial piety and brotherly respect are also auspicious signs among men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet filial piety and brotherly devotion are also auspicious signs among human beings.

sentences.zh: 表門賜爵，勸乃錫類。

translations.literal: Marking the gate and bestowing nobility—by encouraging one, benefits are extended to one's kind.
translations.idiomatic: To honor a household's gate and bestow rank is to encourage virtue and extend its blessings to all of one's kind.

sentences.zh: 彼禽者梟，傷仁害義。

translations.literal: That bird the owl injures benevolence and harms righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: As for that bird, the owl—it injures benevolence and harms righteousness.
